item.title: VPOD-SSP against the increase in VAT for the 13th AVS pension payment
item.description: VPOD-SSP rejects funding the 13th AVS pension payment through a VAT increase, popular vote on November 29; AVS profits of 5.6 billion in 2024 and 4.4 billion in 2025, assets of 60.4 billion.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - VPOD-SSP rejects financing through a VAT increase - The popular vote is scheduled for 29 novembre - The AVS has profits of over 10 billion in two years - The increase would cost 180 francs per family
## Key facts - Who: VPOD-SSP - What: financing the 13th AVS pension through a VAT increase - When: popular vote on 29 novembre - Where: delegates' assembly meeting in Zurich - Decision: 22 votes to 6 - AVS profits: 5,6 billion in 2024 and 4,4 billion in 2025 - Assets: 60,4 billion, equal to 113% of annual expenditure - Average cost: 180 francs more per year per family
On 26 settembre 2026, in Zurich, VPOD-SSP decided to recommend rejecting the financing of the 13th AVS pension through a VAT increase, which will be put to a popular vote on 29 novembre. The decision was taken by the delegates' assembly by 22 votes to 6, as reported in a statement issued today.
The trade union considers additional short-term financing unjustified. The reason given is the state of the AVS's finances, which VPOD-SSP describes as very solid. The organization therefore maintains that there is no sufficient reason to resort immediately to an increase in value-added tax.
### The figures cited by the trade union
In 2024, the AVS is said to have recorded profits of 5,6 billion francs, while profits in 2025 are said to have amounted to 4,4 billion. VPOD-SSP thus speaks of over 10 billion in two years. It adds a record asset base of 60,4 billion, equal to 113% of annual expenditure.
The trade union compares these amounts with the revenue expected from the VAT increase: 1,5 billion francs per year for six years. In its assessment, the profits accumulated over two years would exceed what the tax increase would yield during the period indicated.
The other criticism concerns the nature of VAT, which VPOD-SSP calls an antisocial and regressive tax. The increase would be the second in four years and would cost an average of 180 francs more per year per family. The trade union also argues that the measure would fuel inflation, add to increases in health-insurance premiums, and reduce purchasing power.
Finally, VPOD-SSP invokes the consistency of the trade-union position. During the campaign for the 13th AVS pension, it had been asserted that additional financing would not be necessary; for the long term, by contrast, an increase in wage contributions rather than in VAT had been advocated. For the trade union, raising the tax would represent a victory for employers. For a cross-border worker following the news from Canton Ticino, the first practical point coincides with the source's limitation: the text discusses the financing of the 13th AVS pension and the effect attributed to VAT, but does not address the G permit, withholding tax, LPP, LAMal, rebates, INPS, double taxation, Brogeda or the new 2026 tax agreement. This news therefore cannot be used to derive a new tax or social-security procedure for those crossing the border.
The figure of 180 francs is presented as an annual average per family. It is not an individual deduction, it is not an amount relating to a payslip, and the source does not specifically attribute it to cross-border workers. A worker therefore cannot automatically turn that figure into a change in their monthly net pay. The point made by VPOD-SSP is the general effect on purchasing power, together with inflation and increases in health-insurance premiums.
### The comparison that remains open
| Hypothesis | What can be inferred from the source | What is not indicated | |---|---|---| | Increase in VAT | VPOD-SSP calls it antisocial and regressive | Rate, effective date and individual cost | | Wage contributions | The union advocates them as a long-term solution | Specific level and amount of contributions | | Family expenses | The increase would cost an average of 180 francs per year per family | Breakdown of the cost among individual workers |
If the proposal were not approved, the source does not describe what financing would take its place immediately. It only indicates the union's preference for an increase in wage contributions in the long term. If the financing were approved, the text speaks of an increase in VAT, but specifies neither the rate nor the application date.
This distinction also helps to read the debate correctly from the perspective of a cross-border worker: the source does not announce changes to the G permit, LPP or LAMal and does not link the vote to rebates, INPS, double taxation, Brogeda or the new 2026 tax agreement. To assess the impact indicated by the union on the family budget, the news can be considered alongside [costo della vita Ticino vs Italia](nav:cost-of-living), without turning the average of 180 francs into a personal calculation not provided by the source.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). The safest way to approach the consultation, while staying within the available data, is a reading checklist. The source does not indicate documents to present, polling places or administrative procedures: it therefore makes it possible to organize the information, but not to reconstruct an official procedure.
### Checklist before 29 November
1. Mark the date of the popular vote: 29 November. The subject is the financing of the 13th AHV pension through an increase in VAT.
2. Distinguish the recommendation from the outcome. VPOD-SSP calls for rejecting the financing, but the source does not report the result of the vote. The decision already documented is that of the delegates' assembly held in Zurich, approved by 22 votes to 6.
3. Keep the figures separate. In your notes you can report AHV surpluses of 5,6 billion in 2024 and 4,4 billion in 2025, assets of 60,4 billion equal to 113% of annual expenditure, the stated return of 1,5 billion per year for six years and the estimate of 180 francs per family.
4. Do not confuse the family average with your personal position. The text does not provide a figure for an individual cross-border worker, does not indicate a change in withholding tax and does not describe effects on a G permit, LPP, LAMal, rebates, INPS or double taxation.
5. Compare the two approaches expressed in the source: on the one hand, financing through VAT, criticized as a short-term measure; on the other, an increase in wage contributions, indicated by VPOD-SSP as a long-term solution.
To keep this discussion separate from your individual pension position, you can consult guide [pensione AVS/LPP](nav:pension). For the administrative aspects of cross-border work, comparison [Permesso G/B](nav:permits) remains available, while the news item examined introduces no changes to these tools. Finally, to check your payslip situation, use [calcolatore fiscale](nav:calculator).

item.title: Closure of Erba maternity unit: League inquiry
item.description: Eugenio Zoffili questions Minister Schillaci and calls for technical working groups and exemptions to keep the Erba maternity unit operational.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The maternity unit in Erba is scheduled to close - Eugenio Zoffili has submitted a parliamentary question - The request includes technical working groups and possible exemptions - The area mentioned includes Erbese, Vallassina and Triangolo Lariano
## Key facts - Facility → maternity unit of Erba Hospital - Main figure → Eugenio Zoffili - Addressee → Health Minister Schillaci - Party → Lega Salvini Premier - Area → Erbese, Vallassina and Triangolo Lariano - Parameter → 500 births per year - Requested solutions → technical working groups and exemption mechanisms
The forthcoming closure of the maternity unit at Erba Hospital has reached Parliament through a parliamentary question addressed to Health Minister Schillaci. It was submitted by Eugenio Zoffili, a deputy from Como and group leader of Lega Salvini Premier on Erba City Council. This position was taken after news of the forthcoming closure of the maternity unit, which Zoffili intends to oppose by asking that all solutions useful for keeping it operational be examined.
«The maternity unit at Erba Hospital must not be touched.» With these words, Zoffili reiterated that he had personally asked the owners several times to take a step back and to verify with Regione Lombardia whether an exemption was possible. The question to the minister stems from the same objective: to examine every useful solution to prevent the closure of the maternity unit.
### The two working groups requested by Zoffili
In the text of the question, the deputy specifically points to the opportunity to open a technical working group between the Government and the Region. This should be accompanied by a local working group involving all interested parties: mayors, administrators, trade unions and associations. Zoffili says he has already asked the Mayor for the latter, with the aim of concretely verifying the conditions needed to keep the maternity unit operational, including through the exemption mechanisms provided for by law.
The argument concerns a hospital that, according to the account provided, serves a large area: Erbese, Vallassina and Triangolo Lariano. In these areas, Zoffili argues, the proximity of healthcare services is also essential because of the area’s geographical characteristics. The parameter of 500 births per year is recognized as a factor to consider, but not as the only evaluation criterion. The same legislation, he adds, provides for the possibility of exemptions. Parliament has also already highlighted the need to identify solutions capable of guaranteeing safe healthcare services as close as possible to citizens. This is the point also raised in the in-depth analysis on [servizi sanitari](nav:health).
Lega, Zoffili concludes, will continue to work in Parliament and locally to defend the maternity unit and all related services. In his words, the mobilization should continue with the support of the local community, which is asking for opposition to what it calls an unacceptable decision. For a cross-border reader of the news, the practical connection must remain within the boundaries indicated by the source. The text discusses a healthcare facility serving a broad area and describes proximity as a value linked to geography. The matter therefore remains tied to the possible closure of the birth center and the search for a solution to prevent it.
For the cross-border reader, the news does not make it possible to calculate an individual impact. It does, however, make it possible to identify the criterion used in the comparison: distance and the configuration of the territory should be weighed together with the number of births and the safety of the services. The general overview of [servizi sanitari](nav:health) may offer a separate reference, but it does not replace the contents of the parliamentary question.
### The situation before any possible outcome
| Element | What emerges from the source | |---|---| | Status of the matter | The closure is described as imminent and is being challenged | | Numerical assessment | 500 births per year to be considered, but not the only element | | Territorial assessment | The proximity of services matters because of the geographical characteristics | | Solutions indicated | Government-Region discussions, a territorial working group and exemptions |
This distinction avoids two opposite readings. On the one hand, the parameter of 500 births per year is not ignored: Zoffili states that it must be taken into consideration. On the other hand, the position expressed maintains that this figure cannot by itself conclude the assessment, because the area served is broad and the proximity of services is identified as a fundamental element.
The reference to the exemption must also be read precisely. The source recalls the possibility provided for by legislation and asks that its use be verified; it does not, however, present an exemption that has already been obtained. The same applies to the two working groups: they are instruments indicated in the parliamentary question and the territorial request, not an outcome that has already been reported. For those who live in the area described, the concrete issue is therefore the comparison between the numerical criterion, safety and the proximity of services.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). Anyone who wants to follow the matter can adhere to the steps emerging from the parliamentary initiative, without attributing different procedures to the source. The sequence indicated is political and territorial:
1. Start with the request addressed to the owners: take a step back and verify with the Lombardy Region the possibility of an exemption. 2. Separate the institutional level from the local one: on the one hand, the technical working group between the Government and the Region, and on the other, the local working group. 3. Consider the parties already indicated: mayors, administrators, trade unions and associations. Zoffili reports having requested the local working group from the Mayor. 4. Assess maintaining operations using all the elements mentioned: 500 births per year, geographical characteristics, proximity and safety of services, as well as the exemption mechanisms.
### The questions to follow
To stay up to date on the situation, the reader can check whether the owners will reconsider the decision, whether the Government and the Region will open the technical working group, whether the local discussion will be organized and whether an exemption will be considered. These are the developments consistent with the request reported in the source. No forms, documents, contact details or individual deadlines are indicated, however: the initiative described concerns discussions between institutions and local entities.
The community is called upon to support the campaign for the birth center and related services. The source reports that there is currently a call to oppose the decision, but does not describe a specific procedure for participating. To follow updates on the matter, the in-depth article on [servizi sanitari](nav:health) remains available.
For tools dedicated to cross-border work, consult [calcolatore dello stipendio](nav:calculator).

item.title: Varese: gas and water works on three streets until April 2027
item.description: Starting September 28, 2026, Lereti (Gruppo Acinque) will begin work on Via Masolino da Panicale, Pagliano, and Giovannini. No traffic or parking.
item.content:encoded:
The practical meaning of the plan changes depending on the reader's position relative to the three roads. The source provides for a prohibition on transit and parking, with an exception for residents and pedestrians. For a cross-border commuter who has access to one of the roads involved, the decisive factor is therefore the relationship between their destination and the active construction phase: it is not enough to know that the works are in Varese; one must understand which section is affected at that moment.
### A Restriction That Follows Progress
The progressive nature of the intervention changes daily management. The three roads do not have a single common deadline: the plan is divided into three phases, with periods that overlap and with the application of restrictions linked to the progress of the works. This schedule makes it possible to interpret the measure by section, without automatically turning the entire set of roads into a single construction area.
| Element | What it entails | |---|---| | Transit and parking | Prohibited, except for residents and pedestrians | | Progress | Restrictions applied progressively | | Scheduling | Execution subject to unforeseen construction issues | | End of works | Resurfacing of the affected areas |
For those traveling for work, the difference between the phases matters more than the overall duration alone. A planned passage near Masolino da Panicale requires a different reading from one heading toward Pagliano or Giovannini, because each section is associated with its own time window. [mappa dei valichi](nav:border-map) can be used as an additional tool for navigating the border route, while the phase dates remain the reference for the Varese construction site.
### The Expected Benefit After the Construction Work
The restriction is temporary, but the project has a broader infrastructure objective. The complete replacement of the pipes and the transfer of approximately 30 connections accompany the restoration of the road. The new infrastructure will be integrated with more advanced and digitized monitoring and management systems: according to the source, they will help identify any anomalies more quickly, better schedule maintenance and limit new interventions on the roadway over time. For the reader, the comparison is therefore between a phase of regulated access and an expected outcome of greater reliability, safety and reduced water and gas leakage.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). To turn the schedule into a practical decision, it is advisable to follow a short sequence. The data to relate are the street, the date of the phase, and the exception provided for residents and pedestrians.
### Four-step procedure
1. Identify the street of your route and check whether it coincides with Masolino da Panicale, Pagliano or Giovannini. For via Giovannini, the section up to the intersection with via Masolino da Panicale must be considered; for Masolino, the section up to the intersection with via Pagliano applies.
2. Match the date to the correct phase. Phase 1 starts on 28 September 2026 and ends on 30 November 2026; phase 2 concerns via Pagliano from 15 October 2026 to 25 March 2027; phase 3 concerns via Giovannini from 28 October 2026 to 2 April 2027.
3. Distinguish transit and parking from the personal category. The rule reported is a prohibition for both modes, with an exception for residents and pedestrians. A cross-border worker who does not fall into these categories must therefore take into account the limitation indicated for the section concerned.
4. Consider the actual progress of the construction site. The works are carried out progressively, and the schedule is subject to unforeseen construction-site issues. The check must therefore be linked to the relevant phase, without using a single date as an undifferentiated reference for all the streets.
After the completion of the works, the planned operational step is the restoration of the road surfaces by resurfacing the affected areas. The replacement of the pipes and the transfer of the service connections are also linked to infrastructure equipped with digitized monitoring and management systems, designed to identify anomalies more quickly and schedule maintenance.
When the planning also includes a border crossing, the local check can be supplemented by checking waiting times. To complete the planning of the crossing, consult [tempi di attesa ai valichi](nav:border).

item.title: Robbery in Como: Ticino resident arrested
item.description: The 32-year-old Italian, resident in the Bellinzona area, is among the two arrested for the robbery of 90'000 euros on April 24.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- A 32-year-old Italian lived in the Bellinzona area - The last two fugitives from the robbery arrested - The robbery took place on 24 aprile in Como - Gold loot worth approximately 90'000 euros
## Key facts
What → armed robbery at a jewelry store Where → via Asiago, Como When → 24 aprile Arrested → a 32-year-old Italian resident in Switzerland and a 25-year-old Italian from the province of Monza Loot → gold jewelry worth approximately 90'000 euros
### The raid on via Asiago
A 32-year-old Italian resident in Switzerland is among the two people arrested by the Polizia di Stato di Como for the armed robbery carried out at a jewelry store on via Asiago. The man lived in the Bellinzona area, according to Ticinonline. Along with him, a 25-year-old, also Italian and residing in the province of Monza, was handcuffed.
The two arrests concern the robbery carried out on 24 aprile. The report identifies them as the last two fugitives from the robbery. That day, four people arrived in front of the jewelry store in a rented car. One of them stayed waiting in the car, while the others entered the store.
The robbers had a pistol and their faces were covered by balaclavas. Inside, they threatened the employees and smashed the glass display cases with hammers. Within a few minutes, they had therefore removed the contents, consisting of a very large number of gold jewelry items.
The value of the stolen goods was approximately 90'000 euros. The reconstruction describes a rapid and violent action, focused on the display cases and the jewelry kept in the store. The location indicated for the robbery remains the jewelry store on via Asiago, in Como. ## The Mobile Squad's investigation
### The arrests between April and May
Friday's raid fits into a broader investigative context. Before the operation that led to the arrest of the 32-year-old resident in Switzerland and the 25-year-old from the province of Monza, the investigation had already led to the arrest of three other members of the gang, detained in April and May.
The Como Mobile Squad conducted the investigation into the robbery. The investigators' work made it possible to identify and gather important evidence against all the people who took part in the heist and its instigator. The picture reconstructed in the report therefore includes both the perpetrators of the robbery and the person identified as its instigator, without further details on the individual positions.
The investigation did not end with the arrests. During searches following the arrests of the suspects, part of the stolen goods, which had not yet been passed on, was found. The recovered merchandise was returned to the jewelry store, thereby linking the Mobile Squad's activities also to the recovery of some of the stolen goods.
The discovery concerns some of the many gold jewelry items taken from the store. The source does not indicate the number of objects recovered, but specifies that the stolen goods had not yet been passed on and were returned to the jewelry store. These are the elements that complete the picture of the investigation, together with the arrests carried out in the preceding months.
The investigation described by the Como State Police therefore includes the arrests in April and May, Friday's raid and the searches carried out after the arrests. The investigators gathered evidence against the people who took part in the heist and its instigator, while some of the stolen goods returned to the targeted store. ## The documented follow-up
### From recovery to restitution
For the jewelry store on Via Asiago, the concrete outcome already indicated is the restitution of part of the loot. The recovery took place during the searches following the arrests of the suspects. The objects found were part of the gold jewelry stolen and had not yet been fenced. The source states that the goods were returned to the jewelry store.
On the investigative front, the most recent step is the Friday raid, in which the last two fugitives indicated for the heist were taken. The 32‑year‑old Italian residing in the Bellinzona area and the 25‑year‑old Italian residing in the province of Monza join the other three gang members arrested in April and May. The Como Mobile Squad has gathered evidence against the people who participated in the robbery and its mastermind.
The case maintains two explicit territorial references. The robbery was committed on Via Asiago, in Como; one of the two arrested resided in Switzerland, in the Bellinzona area according to what Ticinonline reported. The other arrested was residing in the province of Monza. The link with Ticino indicated in the news concerns therefore the residence of the 32‑year‑old, while the scene of the robbery and the centre of the investigation remain in Como.
For the shop, the documented result is the return of part of the stolen merchandise. For the investigation, the most recent result is the arrest of the two fugitives, after those of the other three gang members. Thus remain linked the developments communicated by the State Police: the Friday raid, the searches following the arrests, the discovery of the loot not yet fenced and its return to the jewelry store.

item.title: Living in Merone and working in Ticino as a cross-border commuter
item.description: Living in Merone and working in Ticino: what changes regarding withholding tax, deductibles of 7.500 and 10.000 euro, AVS, LPP and LAMal.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Agreement signed on 23 dicembre 2020, in force from 1° gennaio 2024 - Old cross-border commuters: exemption of 7.500 euros until 2033 - New cross-border commuters: allowance of 10.000 euros - Employment tax withheld only in Switzerland
## Key facts - Cross-border commuters agreement → signed on 23 dicembre 2020; in force from 1° gennaio 2024 - Italian ratification → Law 83 of 13 giugno 2023 - Old cross-border commuters → exemption of 7.500 euros, transitional regime 2024–2033 - New cross-border commuters → allowance of 10.000 euros - Employment income → withholding tax only in Switzerland
The New Cross-Border Commuters Agreement between Italy and Switzerland was signed on 23 dicembre 2020. Italy ratified it with Law 83 of 13 giugno 2023, and the text entered into force on 1° gennaio 2024. For those who live in Merone and work in Canton Ticino as cross-border commuters, these dates define the framework to be checked before considering a move.
### The dates that separate the two regimes
The stated dividing date is 17 luglio 2023. Anyone who was already a cross-border commuter before that date falls into the category of old cross-border commuters: they benefit from the exemption of 7.500 euros and the transitional regime from 2024 to 2033. New cross-border commuters, on the other hand, have an allowance of 10.000 euros. The first check therefore concerns one’s status on the established date, not only the place of residence or the commute to work.
Regarding employment income, the stated rule is clear: for cross-border commuters, withholding tax is withheld only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit reported in section CE of form 730. This concerns the tax return and can be explored in greater detail in [dichiarazione dei redditi](nav:tax-return), without turning the credit into a second taxation of the same income.
The Italy–Switzerland Convention for the avoidance of double taxation was signed on 9 marzo 1976. Switzerland is not a member of the EU or the EEA: this reference should be kept distinct from the agreement that entered into force in 2024.
Swiss tax rates, including federal and cantonal rates, are established by federal and cantonal laws. At federal level, administration falls under AFC/ESTV, while the cantonal tax administrations are also involved. For the reader from Merone, the review therefore begins with classifying the regime and reading the Swiss payslip together with the Italian tax section. translated text Before deciding whether to move from Merone and work in Ticino, it is worth turning the rules into a personal worksheet. The aim is not to estimate a generic amount, but to arrive at an orderly review of tax regime, payslip, healthcare and tax return.
### Five practical steps
1. Set the reference date. Write down whether you were already a cross-border worker before 17 luglio 2023. This information determines the group to compare: old cross-border workers with an exemption of 7.500 euro and transitional period 2024-2033, or new cross-border workers with an allowance of 10.000 euro.
2. Note the main tax rule. The cross-border worker's employment income is subject to withholding tax only in Switzerland. In the file, keep the reference to the tax credit in the CE section of the 730, which serves to avoid double taxation in Italy. For the tax-return section, use the [dichiarazione dei redditi](nav:tax-return) as a checkpoint.
3. Read the payslip by blocks. Identify AVS/AI/IPG at 5,3%, AD/AC at 1,1% with a cap of CHF 148'200, LAINF between 0,7% and 1,5%, and LPP between 7% and 18% according to the age bracket starting from the 25esimo year. The method prevents confusing contributions, insurance and withholding tax.
4. Check the healthcare position. With the G permit, there is an option right for LAMal. Note the reference adult deductible, ranging between CHF 300 and CHF 2'500, and keep it separate from social-security deductions. The choice must remain consistent with the personal circumstances you are assessing.
5. Complete the real-world comparison. Add the cost of living and the daily commute you will undertake from Merone. If a border crossing such as Brogeda appears among the alternatives, record the actual route and related expenses, without replacing them with an abstract estimate. Then note the IRPEF rates indicated for 2026 and for 2024-2025 income, keeping the Swiss withholding-tax rule distinct.
This sequence makes it possible to arrive at a documented choice without confusing the new agreement with taxation in both countries. To obtain an estimate of the monthly net amount based on the entries provided, use the [calcolatore dello stipendio](nav:calculator).

item.title: Protest in Castiglione d'Intelvi over concrete batching plant
item.description: Over 750 signatures collected in six days against the concrete batching plant and crusher planned in Castiglione d'Intelvi for the Tremezzina Bypass.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - More than 750 signatures collected in six days - Plant and crusher planned in Castiglione d’Intelvi - The protest concerns the location, not the Bypass - Concerns about dust, noise, water and heavy traffic
## Key facts - Project → concrete batching plant with crusher - Location → municipal territory of Castiglione d’Intelvi - Signature collection → more than 750 signatures in six days - Stated duration → six years - Nearby areas → schools, nursing homes and the Oratory of the Madonna del Restello - Portal → intelviradar.it
More than 750 signatures in six days: the mobilization against the proposal for a concrete batching plant in Castiglione d’Intelvi has reached a significant initial threshold. The project also includes a crusher intended to process stones from the excavations. The area identified is populated and not far from schools, nursing homes and places of cultural interest, including the Oratory of the Madonna del Restello.
The Intelvi Valley has thus returned to the center of news coverage because of operations linked to the construction site of the Tremezzina Bypass. After the Cava Citrini affair, which ended positively for residents, attention has shifted to a second plant proposal. A longtime source for the newspaper, whose identifying details are known but who is not identified, describes a protest that has now erupted.
> «An uproar is breaking out in the Intelvi Valley, people have finally realized what a concrete batching plant is! Especially because of the six-year duration specified in the project, noise and environmental pollution, and traffic that will bring the valley to its knees».
The same source recalls that residents had managed to get the first proposed location at Cava Citrini abandoned. After years without any action, it adds, an area at the entrance to Castiglione would now be in preparation. This reference links the new mobilization to the previous protest, shifting attention to the second proposal.
### From concrete production to the crusher
The concrete batching plant is described as an industrial system for storing, measuring out and precisely mixing the ingredients of fresh concrete. Alongside it, the crusher would process the excavated stones. For the proponents, the duration specified in the project, six years, makes the choice of location decisive.
### The protest and its scope
The document circulated by residents specifies that the mobilization is not against the Tremezzina Bypass. The opposition concerns the plant’s location and the anticipated consequences for health, the environment, road traffic, safety and the valley’s tourism and residential character. The concerns include dust and noise, water consumption, possible effects on soil and groundwater, as well as the passage of heavy vehicles carrying stones, concrete and water from the lake. ## How to follow the mobilization
The operational guidelines contained in the document focus on information, participation and institutional dialogue. The channel indicated by citizens is the intelviradar.it portal, activated to ensure transparency, regular updates and access to information about the project and the initiatives.
### From the portal to the assembly
1. Consult intelviradar.it for updates on the project and the mobilization. 2. Learn more on the portal about the reasons for the protest and the issues contested by citizens. 3. Look for information on how to sign the petition promoted by the community. 4. Follow the request for a public assembly with Mario Pozzi, identified as the Mayor of the municipality most affected, and with all representatives of the institutions involved.
The only timeline reported in the source concerns the collection of signatures: more than 750 signatures were reached in six days. This figure measures the speed of the mobilization, but is not presented as a deadline for signing. The document does not indicate a date for the assembly, a deadline for the petition or a work schedule.
To avoid misunderstandings, the organizers’ request should be kept distinct from the main project. The text specifies that the protest does not concern the Variante della Tremezzina, but rather the location of the facility and its possible consequences. Those consulting the portal can therefore focus on the concrete batching plant, the related crusher, the road network and the requests addressed to the administrations.
Citizens are asking institutions and the competent administrations, starting with the Municipalities of the Valley, for greater transparency toward the population and a review of the project. The request is justified by the protection of the environment, public health and the future of Val d’Intelvi. item.title: Robbery at Bennet: alleged mastermind arrested in Ticino
item.description: A 32-year-old resident of the Bellinzona area and a 25-year-old from Monza were arrested for the robbery at the Stroili jewelry store in the Bennet shopping center in Tavernola.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - A 32-year-old resident of the Bellinzona area arrested - A 25-year-old resident in the province of Monza also arrested - Stroili jewelry store at Bennet in Tavernola targeted - Loot estimated at around 90'000 euro
## Key facts - Arrests: Friday 25 settembre - Investigation: Como State Police - Robbery: 24 aprile - Location: Bennet in Tavernola, Como - Detention: Bassone prison
### The arrest in Como On Friday 25 settembre, the Como State Police arrested a 32-year-old Italian man residing in the Bellinzona area as part of the investigation into the armed robbery at the Stroili jewelry store in the Bennet shopping center in Tavernola, Como. According to initial reconstructions, the man was allegedly the mastermind of the criminal group.
In the same operation, a 25-year-old resident of the province of Monza was arrested. The two measures were carried out on the basis of a pre-trial detention order issued by the judge for preliminary investigations in Como at the request of the Public Prosecutor's Office. Both were transferred to the Como prison, the Bassone prison.
The robbery for which the investigation was launched dates back to 24 aprile. Four people, all disguised, had reached the jewelry store in a rental car. One of the members had remained at the wheel, while the other three had entered the shop with their faces covered by balaclavas.
The three who entered the jewelry store were armed with a pistol and had hammers. After threatening the employees with the weapon, they had smashed the glass display cases and taken possession of numerous gold jewelry items. The total value of the goods had been estimated at around 90'000 euro.
The last two arrests came after those of the other three members of the group, carried out by the Como Mobile Squad between April and May. According to the investigation, the case thus involves all the alleged participants in the raid that took place in the Tavernola shopping center. ## The reconstruction of the heist
The robbery at the Stroili jewelry store in Bennet in Tavernola had been prepared using a rental car. Four people were inside, all disguised. One had remained at the wheel; the other three had reached the store to carry out the heist.
Inside the jewelry store, the three had their faces covered by balaclavas and had entered with a pistol and hammers. The employees had been threatened with the weapon. The hammers had been used to smash the glass display cases, from which numerous gold jewelry items had been taken.
The operation had unfolded in a few minutes. Before fleeing, the people who had entered the store had managed to take jewelry with a total estimated value of around 90'000 euros. The robbery had been described as particularly violent and similar to a scene from a Hollywood action film.
### The arrests and the stolen goods
The investigations by the Como Mobile Squad had led to the arrest of the other three members of the group between April and May. Subsequent inquiries had enabled investigators to reconstruct, according to the prosecution, the roles of the various participants.
Investigators had also gathered evidence against the alleged mastermind. During searches carried out after the arrests, part of the stolen goods had been recovered before they could enter the channels for handling stolen goods.
The recovered jewelry had subsequently been returned to the jewelry store. The recovery was one of the developments in the investigation into the robbery of 24 April, together with the evidence collected by the Mobile Squad to reconstruct the roles of the people involved, according to the prosecution. ## The continuation of the investigation
With the arrests carried out on Friday 25 September, the investigation into the 24 April robbery now involves all the alleged participants in the heist. The latest measure concerns the 32-year-old Italian resident in the Bellinzonese area and the 25-year-old resident in the province of Monza, while the other three arrests had already been carried out between April and May.
The two men arrested on Friday were remanded in custody at the Como prison, Bassone. The order was issued by the investigating judge in Como at the request of the Public Prosecutor’s Office. The arrest therefore represents the latest development reported in the investigation by the Como State Police.
### Responsibility still to be established The source specifies that the responsibility of the two arrested men, as well as that of the other suspects, will have to be established during the subsequent stages of the proceedings. This also concerns the role attributed to the 32-year-old: according to initial reconstructions, the man was allegedly the mastermind of the criminal group.
The investigations enabled investigators to reconstruct, according to the prosecution, the roles of the various participants and to gather evidence also against the alleged instigator. These are the elements on which the proceedings will continue after the two men’s transfer to Bassone prison.
The developments already reported also include searches carried out following the arrests and the recovery of part of the stolen goods. The jewelry had been returned to the jewelry store before it could enter the channels for handling stolen goods. The assessment of responsibility remains entrusted to the subsequent stages of the proceedings, as specified for all the suspects.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 12 and 13 September: first edition of Industrial Quest - 46 sites in 15 European countries - Five teams at Cotonificio Cantoni LIUC - Zamponari 40 points, Gli stranieri 35
## Key facts - Promoter → ERIH – European Route of Industrial Heritage - Italian venue → Cotonificio Cantoni, LIUC campus in Castellanza - Local participation → 5 teams - Highest score → Zamponari, 40 points - Second LIUC team → Gli stranieri, 35 points - Pilot edition → 46 sites in 15 countries
On 12 and 13 September, LIUC – Università Cattaneo represented Italy in the first edition of Industrial Quest, the initiative promoted by ERIH – European Route of Industrial Heritage. Italian participation focused on Cotonificio Cantoni, with a route dedicated to traces of its history still visible on the university campus in Castellanza.
The initiative concluded after two days designed to bring the public closer to Europe’s industrial heritage through a participatory and itinerant format. At the various venues, museums, historic production sites and places of industrial memory offered activities to be completed with a smartphone: quizzes, observation exercises, estimation questions, searches for details of buildings and photographic challenges.
### The first Italian challenge
The stated objective was to transform the visit into an active exploration experience. Participants were called upon to look more closely at spaces, architecture, machinery and evidence of the history of work and industry. Each site created its own quest based on the characteristics of the location, while local rankings made it possible to compare the teams’ results.
The pilot edition involved 46 sites in 15 European countries, from Germany to Finland, from Poland to Portugal and as far as Ukraine. In Italy, the initiative came to LIUC – Università Cattaneo for the first time. Castellanza was the only Italian site present in the first edition, and Cotonificio Cantoni LIUC was among the venues with more substantial participation.
Five teams registered at the Italian site. This places the Castellanza venue in a visible position within the European pilot, as it combines Italy’s presence with the response from the groups that chose the route dedicated to the cotton mill.
The score rankings also produced a positive result. «Zamponari», captained by LIUC lecturer Laura Cattaneo and winner of the local ranking, finished with 40 points, entering the upper part of the European ranking for individual performances. «Gli stranieri», the second LIUC team, obtained 35 points and placed in the same tier.
The outcome of the first edition is therefore twofold: the Cantoni-LIUC site attracted substantial participation in numerical terms, and two teams reached the upper tier of the European comparison. ## In brief - On-board ticket: 3,20 euro in the attached receipt - Card not working, according to the student - From 23 settembre, access, traffic flow and parking change - Insubria indicates lines C, E and reinforcement services

The on-board ticket purchased on a bus heading to the Bizzozero university campus cost 3,20 euro according to the receipt attached to the report. The amount is double the normal fare indicated by the student.
The student at Università dell'Insubria wrote to VareseNews. She and some classmates had not bought the ticket in advance and were not subscribers: they thought they could purchase it on board.
On board, however, the card payment device was not working, according to her account. “It was therefore only possible to buy the ticket with coins,” the student recounts. The driver issued the tickets, applying the surcharge provided for those who had not purchased them beforehand and did not have a pass.
### The fare applied
The surcharge for purchasing on board is provided for by the service rules. Therefore, formally speaking, the driver's behavior is not an anomaly. The letter instead raises a question about occasional access: how easy is it to use the bus in Varese without being regular users?
In the reported case, it was possible to buy the ticket on board, but card payment was not available on the service in question, leaving coins as the only option. The receipt made the effect of the surcharge visible: 3,20 euro.

The report comes as the Bizzozero Campus changes its access, traffic flow and parking arrangements. From 23 settembre, new arrangements linked to work for new parking areas and, later, a multifunctional building came into force.
Università dell'Insubria invited students and staff, whenever possible, to favor public transport. It points to urban lines C and E and the additional services of the university reinforcement service as alternatives to the car.
The university is also continuing the Bus Insubria service between central Varese and Bizzozero, carpooling, and agreements for shared bicycles and scooters. The initiatives dedicated to university mobility focus on the Varese Campus and the need to reduce the number of cars heading to the campus every day. ## The point for those who use the service occasionally
The report separates two aspects that often end up in the same incident. On the one hand, there is a fare rule: a ticket bought on board entails a surcharge. On the other, there is the experience of a user who decides to take the bus without a pass and encounters electronic payment unavailable on the service described. The rule may be applied correctly, but the service may be less straightforward for those who use it only occasionally.

The useful comparison is not between those who respected or violated a rule. In the case described, no one disputes that the surcharge is provided for. item.description: A reader's letter reports an echo or vibration every time a car drives on state road 707, audible in three areas of Varese, and asks ANAS when it will be resolved.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Barriers installed on state road 707 - Noise every time cars pass - Sounds audible in three areas of Varese - Appeal to ANAS: when will it be resolved?
## Key facts - Intervention → sound-absorbing barriers - Road → state road 707 - Purpose → reduce the noise of passing cars - Locations indicated → via Goldoni, viale Borri and largo Flaiano - Reported effect → echo/vibration every time a car passes - Recipient of the appeal → ANAS
The installation of sound-absorbing barriers on state road 707 is at the center of a report addressed to ANAS. The intervention, carried out to reduce the noise caused by cars traveling along Varese's motorway link, is described by the reader as a paradoxical case: instead of decreasing, the noise would have become extremely bothersome.
The letter received and published also indicates where the phenomenon would be perceptible. The sound is heard in via Goldoni, viale Borri and largo Flaiano. The description therefore links the problem to a specific stretch of road and to three explicitly named points in the city, without extending the report to other areas.
### The account contained in the letter
The passage described is always the same: a car passes, noise is produced, and the noise can be heard in the streets mentioned. The reader is not speaking only of an occasional disturbance, but of an effect that recurs every time cars pass. In the reader's account, the barrier installed to absorb the sound would therefore be associated with an acoustic response opposite to the purpose of the intervention.
> “I suspect an error in the installation of the sound-absorbing barriers, which produces an annoying echo/vibration whenever a car passes.”
The hypothesis concerns an installation error. It is the reader who links that error to the echo or vibration; the sentence is presented as an assumption within an appeal, not as the result of a technical assessment reported in the text.
The final point of the letter is a request to ANAS, made through the newspaper: when will the problem be resolved? The question reflects the practical nature of the report. It does not ask for a general explanation about the barriers, but for an answer regarding the disturbance produced by their effect, as perceived when cars pass.
The news therefore remains anchored to three elements: the intervention on state road 707, the reported acoustic effect and the request for a solution. The source presents the text as a reader's letter received and published. The heart of the report is the contrast between the stated purpose of the barriers and the experience described in the streets near the link road. ## What it means for those traveling through Varese

The term sound-absorbing identifies the intended function of the intervention: reducing noise. The reader instead describes the opposite effect, with an extremely annoying sound every time a vehicle passes. This opposition is the practical key to the case: the report does not challenge the idea of barriers in the abstract, but asks for a solution to what, according to the writer, occurred after their installation.

item.title: Smart working for cross-border workers: 25% limit on days
item.description: The tax threshold for smart working from Italy is 25%; entered into force on 9 febbraio 2026, retroactive application from 1 gennaio 2024. One day out of five is 20%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The tax threshold for smart working from Italy is 25% - The protocol entered into force on 9 February 2026 - The application is retroactive from 1 January 2024 - In five days, one day of teleworking counts as 20%
## Key facts - Tax threshold → 25% - Entry into force → 9 February 2026 - Retroactive application → 1 January 2024 - One day out of five → 20% - Two days per week → 40%
On 9 February 2026, the protocol governing the teleworking of cross-border workers definitively entered into force. The rule concerns those who work for a Swiss company but carry out part of their work from their home in Italy, without crossing the border every day.
The threshold indicated by the agreement between Italy and Switzerland is 25% of working time. Within this limit, days worked from home are considered, for the purposes of the taxation provided for under the agreement, as days worked at the Swiss employer's premises. The point is therefore not only where the worker is located on a particular day, but what proportion of the total time is worked from Italy.
The protocol is no longer tied to a temporary measure. Its application is retroactive from 1 January 2024, while its definitive entry into force took place on 9 February 2026. The short answer provided by the source therefore concerns the tax threshold applicable to work carried out from an Italian home.
### What the threshold establishes
The measure concerns the tax status of a cross-border worker. A worker may carry out up to 25% of their work from their home in Italy without this, within that threshold, changing their tax status as a cross-border worker. The source also specifies that the rule applies to workers covered by the transitional regime for so-called «old cross-border workers».
The practical interpretation is indicative: 25% corresponds to one day per week. However, the correct calculation must be made based on total working time and not simply by counting weeks. In a five-day working week, one day of teleworking equals 20% of working time; two days per week, on the other hand, correspond to 40% and exceed the 25% tax threshold.
For a cross-border worker who works for a Swiss employer, this is the distinction to bear in mind: the agreement allows work from home in Italy within the percentage limit, whereas an arrangement that exceeds the limit indicated by the source does not fall within the tax threshold described. For an initial check, the figure can be compared with [calcolatore fiscale](nav:calculator), keeping the calculation of time separate from the assessment of income. For the cross-border worker, the practical difficulty is not reading the number 25%, but turning it into a weekly arrangement without confusing the percentage with a fixed number of days. The source actually indicates that the correct calculation must be made based on total working time and not simply by counting weeks. The reference to one day per week is therefore indicative: it serves as a guide, but does not replace the ratio between the time worked from Italy and the total activity.
For a five-day working week, the examples provided make the transition clear:
| Arrangement | Share of working time | Interpretation with respect to 25% | |---|---:|---| | One day of telework | 20% | Within the indicated threshold | | Two days of telework | 40% | Above the indicated threshold |
One day out of five does not equal 25%, but 20%. Two days out of five amount to 40%. Therefore, the question to ask is not only how many days are spent at home, but what percentage they represent of the total working time. In the case of a five-day week, the comparison does not require turning 25% into another figure: the values provided are enough to distinguish the limit from its practical translation.
### The calendar must be read together with the share
A cross-border worker who performs part of their activity from their home in Italy may use the calendar as a starting point, but must then relate that figure to the total amount of work. If the arrangement follows a five-day week, one day remains at 20%, while two rise to 40%. In the latter case, the 25% tax threshold is exceeded according to the example indicated by the source.
The rule also applies to workers who fall under the transitional regime of the so-called «old cross-border workers». For this group, the figure to monitor remains the 25% tax threshold for activity carried out from the home in Italy. The parameter is therefore the share of working time, not simply the name assigned to the day spent at home.
This distinction helps prevent attributing to the calendar a meaning it does not have: the week provides an example, while the parameter is total working time. To connect the calculation of the share with the reading of net pay, [simulatore busta paga](nav:payslip) can be used, keeping the count of days separate from the tax result.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). An operational check can remain within the data indicated by the source. The cross-border worker starts from the total working time and builds the comparison progressively, without relying solely on counting the weeks.
### Five steps to check the percentage
1. Define the total working time to be considered. It is the basis of the calculation: the source establishes that one must not limit oneself to counting the weeks.
2. Isolate the smart-working days worked from home in Italy. They are the part of the activity to which the telework rule for cross-border workers applies.
3. Relate them to the total and check the 25%. Up to this percentage, days worked from home are considered, for the purposes of the taxation provided for by the agreement, as days worked at the Swiss employer's workplace.
4. If the working week is five days, compare the result with the examples available: one day equals 20% of the working time, two days 40%.
5. Check whether you fall under the transitional regime of the so-called «old cross-border workers». The source specifies that the 25% rule also applies to this category.
The time-related data must be read together with the calculation. The protocol definitively entered into force on 9 February 2026, but applies retroactively from 1 January 2024. These dates place the rules within the period indicated by the source and help to correctly interpret the rule on working from home in Italy.
If the planning does not follow an identical week, the reference nevertheless remains the total time: the value of one day per week is indicative and does not replace the calculation of the share. For the next step on the tax issue, [dichiarazione dei redditi](nav:tax-return) is available. To estimate your own situation, finally use [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator).

item.title: Assaults and violent nights: young people from Ticino tell their stories
item.description: On 1 August 2025, a 19-year-old from Bellinzona was beaten under Mario Botta’s shelter; in 2024, the juvenile justice system opened 912 case files; Taha, 24, is awaiting deportation after a sentence of 2 years and 6 months in Kloten prison.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - On 1° agosto 2025, a 19-year-old was beaten under the shelter. - In 2024, the juvenile justice system opened 912 case files. - Taha, 24, is awaiting expulsion from Switzerland. - Summer news reports followed one another almost every day.
## Key facts - Date → 1° agosto 2025 - Location → Mario Botta bus shelter - Victim → 19-year-old from Bellinzona - Taha's sentence → 2 years and six months in detention - Taha's prison → Kloten administrative detention center
On 1° agosto 2025, under the Mario Botta bus shelter, a 19-year-old from Bellinzona was punched and kicked by the group while he was lying on the ground. The incident is described as the most serious in recent times.
Fights and beatings mark the nights in Ticino, where summer crime reports followed one another at an almost daily pace. On a Saturday evening in April, some minors who hang around the bus shelter in Lugano describe what they see every weekend. “You see them every weekend,” one of them says. “They face off in gangs, in groups.”
The description also includes the presence of weapons. “Two boys were arguing; at a certain point, one of them pulled out a knife,” a minor recounts. The remarks come from an evening during which the youths talk about groups, gangs and clashes. The shelter is mentioned again in the case of the 19-year-old from Bellinzona, attacked by the group while he was already on the ground.
### Taha's account
Taha is 24, was born in Iraq and arrived in Ticino as a refugee. Today, he is awaiting expulsion. His is not the account of a victim: for years, he was a violent attacker and never managed to curb his aggression.
“Violence was the worst problem I have ever had,” he says. He then sums up his attitude at the time: “I was immature, I was proud.”
Four years ago, he was sentenced to 2 years and six months in detention for an assault at the Locarno roundabout, the final episode of a turbulent adolescence. The young man speaks from behind the bars of the Kloten administrative detention center and links his aggression to the upbringing he received. “I was raised with violence,” he says. For this reason, violence appeared to him for a long time as the best solution to every problem. His story accompanies the account of the nights in Ticino and of an assault that, under the Mario Botta bus shelter, left a 19-year-old on the ground amid punches and kicks. In 2024, the juvenile justice authorities opened 912 case files, 18 percent more than the previous year. Over ten years, investigations increased by 37 percent. Residents, business owners and merchants are concerned about news reports dominated by brawls, beatings and stabbings.
### The figure concerning minors and the alarm in Lugano
Luana Riva has lived in Molino Nuovo for years and today denounces a situation she considers out of control. «This has become the Bronx», she says. The woman witnessed a brutal beating that took place on via Trevano, for no apparent reason. A few dozen metres away, she also points out the site of a stabbing.
Her protest directly concerns the city's safety. «Is Lugano safe? Let a city councillor come and tell me that to my face!», she says furiously. Then she adds: «I'll offer him room and board and let him stay at my house for a week. Then he'll understand».
According to the boys interviewed at the bus shelter, the reasons for brawls can be trivial. A boy dressed in black from head to toe observes: «If you bother someone, it's normal for a fight to break out». And he adds: «If you talk about someone else's girl, then what has to happen happens».
Not everyone, however, considers Lugano a dangerous city. Another boy, holding a bottle of prosecco, comments: «You just have to avoid looking for trouble».
Giulio experienced violence firsthand. He was attacked by two young men in the middle of Piazza Grande in Locarno, over one look too many. After that incident, he says: «For a year or two, I stopped going out. If it happened once, it can happen again».
A surveillance camera will make it possible to reconstruct the events and nail the attackers, two Syrian brothers. Giulio does not hide his resentment: «I don't forgive them». To the boys, however, he sends a message opposed to fear: «Go out! You are not the ones who should limit your freedom. The problem isn't you; the problem is violent people».
### The stories of Fabio and Matteo
Fabio, a pseudonym, accumulated around sixty charges during his adolescence, including assault, theft and extortion. He was one of the main figures in the massive brawl that broke out at the mouth of the Cassarate during lockdown. Two years and eight months in a community in Italy brought him back to a normal life. Looking back, he says: «As a child, I had to learn to survive. My mother wasn't even capable of cooking for me; I had to steal to eat».
Matteo had a similar path, marked by beatings, brawls and punches. He remembers the rivalry between groups: one spoke badly of the other, and arguments turned into feuds. Today he has left violence behind and reflects with detachment on what happened. «It stemmed from a deep inner sadness», he explains. «If you wanted to be the centre of attention, the easiest way was to use violence».
The statistics concerning minors, the residents' words and the accounts of those who went through those experiences paint a local picture in which concern coexists with different explanations: alcohol, pride, peer pressure and deeper suffering. Hitting people for fun, as a pastime or out of boredom. The latest incidents that occurred during the Ticino carnivals also seem to confirm this drift: gangs of hooded and armed teenagers, ready to start a brawl and throw punches for no reason.
### The ambushes during the carnivals
Some young victims ended up in the emergency room. The victims or their parents describe ambushes and completely gratuitous violence. In accounts of the Ticino evenings, the assault therefore does not always arise from an already open confrontation: in some cases, the gangs seem to prepare to strike without any explanation.
### Music, artists and controversial role models
Taha observes that young people's aggressiveness follows the fashion of music and artists and the gangster game. He himself admits to having been influenced by certain controversial role models.
Fabio also speaks of an excessive trivialization of violence. «It's fashionable, violence is fashionable,» he says. In his view, this attitude seems to stem from trap songs, «which talk only about weapons, drugs, money».
Matteo considers those contents particularly influential on young people already adrift. «If you listen to the lyrics of today's songs, they always talk about weapons, drugs, power,» he says. And he adds: «A boy aged 12 to 17 who listens only to music like this is influenced by it».
### The still-disputed expulsion
«The situation is getting worse and worse,» observes Taha, who knows the Ticino nights and their more hot-headed attendees well. At only 24, he dreams of a quiet domestic life, but disputes the expulsion. He says he has paid for what he did and would like to demonstrate that the path of redemption has been effective. Today he assures that he is a new and better person.
The step he is awaiting is the arrival of the travel documents. As soon as they arrive, he will have to leave Switzerland for an Iraq he does not know and where he has no ties. His future remains tied to that departure, while the young man continues to maintain that violence belongs to the past.
Taha closes his account with a melancholy smile: «Everything is getting worse, but good people exist. You just have to find them».

## Two aspects to keep separate
For a cross-border worker who works in Canton Ticino, the move to the Council of States should be read alongside the rules already applicable, without automatically turning it into a tax change. The source discusses Bilaterals III and a Switzerland-EU package; it does not present the dossier as a new 2026 tax agreement. This distinction avoids attributing immediate effects to a payslip or a permit.
The New Cross-Border Commuter Agreement has its own timeline: it was signed on 23 dicembre 2020 and has been in force since 1 gennaio 2024. These dates belong to the framework already applicable and are not indicated by the source as part of the announced review. The comparison can be read as follows:

The most concrete point for taxation therefore remains separate: withholding tax on employment income is withheld only in Switzerland, while Italy avoids double taxation through a tax credit in section CE of the 730. The text on Bilaterals III does not announce a change to this mechanism.

The same caution applies to AVS, LPP and LAMal. ### Checklist for the cross-border worker
1. Note the timeframe: starting Monday, the package will be examined by the Council of States. This is the journalistic deadline indicated by the source, not an individual tax deadline.
2. When reading an update, distinguish the debate from any possible decision. The source speaks of expected sparks and a marathon debate, but does not communicate a definitive outcome.

## In brief - SIMEX 26 took place on Thursday evening in Agno - An aircraft accident in the airport area was simulated - Alarms, emergency services and coordination were tested - The airport’s Crisis Committee was reviewed

### The exercise scenario
On Thursday evening, Agno airport hosted SIMEX 26, a large-scale emergency exercise. The test had a precise objective: to test safety procedures and coordination among the various agencies in the event of an emergency at the airport.
The scenario prepared for the exercise simulated an aircraft accident in the airport area. Multiple people were involved in the simulation, and one of the access points normally used by emergency vehicles was temporarily unavailable. The exercise scenario therefore included the simulated aircraft event, the involvement of multiple people and the temporary unavailability of an access point.
The exercise covered the alarm chain, the intervention of emergency services and coordination between the airport and first-response organizations. SIMEX 26 linked these three elements within the scenario defined for Agno, verifying how the planned response was coordinated between the airport and the agencies involved.
The description is contained in a statement published on Friday by the City of Lugano. The text links the exercise to the verification of safety procedures and coordination in the event of an emergency. The temporary unavailability of an access point normally used by emergency vehicles was part of the simulated situation, as was the involvement of multiple people.
The objective was not to report an accident that had actually occurred, but to test the organized response to an airport emergency scenario. For this reason, the exercise brought together alarms, emergency services and coordination between the airport and first-response organizations, with the Crisis Committee and communications listed among the additional checks. ## Operational checks

The exercise examined several functions within the same scenario. The note first indicates the alarm chain, which was tested together with the response of the emergency services. The City of Lugano also reports on the functioning of the airport's Crisis Committee. This element too was verified during the exercise. The Crisis Committee therefore appears alongside the alarm chain, emergency services and coordination as part of the activities tested at Agno.

### From simulation to evaluation
For SIMEX 26, the follow-up indicated by the source concerns the analysis of the results. The exercise took place under the supervision of the Federal Office of Civil Aviation, referred to by the acronym UFAC, and the results will be analyzed and evaluated in the coming weeks.
UFAC supervision accompanied the simulation at Agno Airport. The next phase, however, is devoted to reviewing the results of the exercise. The test put security procedures, the alarm chain, the intervention of emergency services, and coordination between the airport and first-response organizations to the test. item.description: From 1° gennaio 2027, the federal mandate passes from AOZ to ORS Service; the VPOD and OCST unions warn of up to 40 layoffs in Chiasso and Pasture among 120 AOZ Ticino employees.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The federal mandate will move from AOZ to ORS as of 1° gennaio 2027 - 40 jobs at risk between Chiasso and Pasture - AOZ Ticino has 120 employees
- Federal mandate — from AOZ to ORS Service as of 1° gennaio 2027 - Centers affected — Pasture and Chiasso - AOZ Ticino staff — 120 employees - Worst-case scenario — 40 layoffs - Current contract — collective labor agreement - Unions — VPOD and OCST - Meeting — extraordinary meeting with AOZ Ticino staff
Forty layoffs are the worst-case scenario indicated by the VPOD union for the reorganization of the Federal Asylum Center in Pasture and Chiasso. The change already defined concerns the federal mandate: as of 1° gennaio 2027, it will move from AOZ to ORS Service.
### The meeting with the staff
The prospect worries the unions, which organized an extraordinary meeting with AOZ Ticino staff. There are 120 employees. The meeting is intended to discuss the changes within the facilities with them and the possible consequences for employment.
The co-secretary of VPOD Ticino, Edoardo Cappelletti, links the possibility of the 40 layoffs to the Chiasso Center not reopening. According to the union, ORS will not be able to absorb all of AOZ's employees, and a reduction in employment has already been suggested. If Chiasso were not to reopen, VPOD's estimate is that around forty employees would be left without work. Cappelletti describes the prospect as burdensome, serious and irresponsible, especially for the Mendrisio and Chiasso region.
> «It has already been suggested that ORS will not be able to absorb all of AOZ's employees», says Cappelletti.
OCST is also supporting the cause. Regional deputy secretary Nenad Jovanovic explains that the consultation aims first and foremost to minimize the number of people affected by a possible loss of employment: the proposed solution is redeployment with the new employer or in other areas through the procedure. If layoffs were to occur, OCST is calling for a serious social plan to support people in their search for new employment.
The discussion also concerns the contract. AOZ employees are currently covered by a collective labor agreement. With the change at the top, this certainty disappears: according to Cappelletti, ORS does not intend to take over the agreement signed by VPOD. The union therefore fears a deterioration in working conditions and the dismantling of the rights obtained through the staff commission. For those following cross-border work, the directly documented point concerns employment. The news concerns jobs at two facilities in Ticino and a transition of the mandate from AOZ to ORS Service. For a cross-border worker who was among the personnel involved, the issue would therefore be continuity of employment and working conditions, not effects on other areas that the source does not mention.
### The comparison before and after
| Item | Situation described | |---|---| | Mandate management | AOZ; from 1 January 2027 ORS Service | | Contract | Collective agreement for AOZ employees; ORS does not intend to take it over | | Redeployment | With the new employer or in other areas | | Job loss | The union is calling for a serious social plan |
The transition therefore has two levels. The first is quantitative: how many jobs remain after the change of operator. The second is qualitative: under which contract and working conditions the work continues. Even redeployment, in the logic set out by OCST, does not eliminate the question of the conditions applied by the new employer. Likewise, job loss is not presented as an outcome already decided: it is the scenario that the unions want to contain through consultation, redeployment and a social plan.
Chiasso remains the turning point. VPOD links the failure to reopen to the possibility of around forty people being left without work. The source does not, however, present a definitive outcome regarding the reopening; therefore, the estimate cannot be turned into a dismissal that has already been decided. For those who have to assess their own position, the difference between a hypothesis, consultation and a decision is essential.
There is also the issue of service quality, mentioned alongside the defense of employment and working conditions. Cappelletti challenges the criterion by which the Federal Council awarded the public contract: according to the union, the lowest price was not accompanied by clear and binding criteria on employment continuity and working conditions. The debate therefore concerns both the continuity of jobs and the way in which the service will be organized.
Those seeking new employment can meanwhile consult the [annunci di lavoro](nav:jobs), without considering this tool as an outcome already imposed by the reorganization.

### The steps indicated by the consultation
1. Follow the extraordinary assembly organized with the AOZ Ticino staff. This is the venue designated for discussing the reorganization within the facilities.
2. Bring the issue of reassignment into the consultation, either to the new employer or in other sectors, as indicated by OCST. The stated objective is to minimize the number of people affected by job loss.
3. If dismissal is put on the table, request that a serious social plan be evaluated. OCST identifies this as a support tool for those who will have to seek new employment.
4. Follow the approval of the Staff Assembly's resolution. The topics indicated are the defense of employment, working conditions, and service quality.
5. Verify the addressees to whom the resolution will be directed: the AOZ Board of Directors, the State Secretariat for Migration, the State Council, and the Ticino delegation to the Federal Assembly.
