item.title: Como, fugitive from the Campione robbery arrested
item.description: Dario De Bernardi, 55 years old, was arrested on 23 settembre: he must serve over 19 years and is identified as the perpetrator of the 750.000-franc robbery in Campione.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Dario De Bernardi, 55, was arrested on September 23 - Was wanted since 2011 and must serve over 19 years - He is indicated as the executor of the robbery at the Champion Casino
## Key facts - Person → Dario De Bernardi, 55 years old, originally from the province of Lecco - Stop in the → afternoon of 23 September - Penalty of → more than 19 years imprisonment - Robbery → 28 March 2018, with 750,000 Swiss francs stolen - Destination → Casa Circondariale di Como
### The arrest after the long escape In the afternoon of September 23, the Carabinieri of the Provincial Command of Como put an end to the long escape of Dario De Bernardi, 55, originally from the province of Lecco. The man, wanted since 2011, was identified and arrested at the end of an extensive investigation coordinated by the Public Prosecutor's Office of Como.
A detention order issued in 2016 by the General Prosecutor's Office at the Court of Appeal of Milan hung over De Bernardi. The measure was aimed at serving a sentence of more than 19 years in prison for crimes including association aimed at drug trafficking, robbery and more.
The 55-year-old was also wanted since 2019 following an order of pre-trial detention in prison issued by the GIP of the Court of Como. The order was part of the investigations conducted by the Carabinieri of the Provincial Command of Como and directed by the Como Public Prosecutor's Office.
The picture ## The case of the robbery at the Casino ### The escape and the 2018 proceedings De Bernardi’s fugitive status had begun in 2011 and, according to the reconstruction, had led him to move to various locations. Possible stays abroad are also indicated, before a recent residence presumably identified in the Larian Province. The escape thus unfolded through multiple movements, while the man remained beyond the reach of justice.
The second aspect of the matter concerns the armed robbery on 28 March 2018 targeting Casinò Campione d’Italia. Investigations conducted by the Carabinieri of the Como Provincial Command and directed by the Como Prosecutor’s Office had identified De Bernardi as the person who physically carried out the assault. During the robbery, 750,000 Swiss francs were stolen.
The incident took place during the period when the 55-year-old was already a fugitive. For this reason, after the investigative activities, De Bernardi had been referred to the authorities as untraceable. His position differed from that of the other participants in the action, who were subsequently arrested by the Carabinieri.
A few months after the robbery, still in 2018, the officers had in fact arrested the wanted man’s three accomplices. The source specifies that all three were later convicted. De Bernardi, on the other hand, had not been arrested and had continued to evade justice.
In 2019, the search for him had also become linked to a pre-trial detention order in prison issued by the preliminary investigations judge of the Como Court. That measure arose from the investigation into the robbery at the Casino in Campione and was added to the order to enforce the sentence issued in 2016 for a term exceeding 19 years. The legal matter therefore includes the proceedings for the armed assault and the earlier order to enforce the sentence. ## The Capture and Search ### Among Firewood and Construction Debris The capture operation began on the afternoon of September 23. The soldiers of the Investigative Unit located De Bernardi, followed him, and then stopped him on a public street, catching him by surprise and preventing him from resisting. After being detained, the man was taken to the Provincial Command.
The subsequent phase took place with the support of the Carabinieri of the Calabria Airborne Squadron. The soldiers carried out a thorough search of the premises of a residence in the province of Como recently used by De Bernardi. The operation focused on the areas where stacked firewood and construction debris were present.
Precisely in that area, perfectly concealed, two items were found. The first was a hunting rifle held illegally. The second consisted of a total sum of 98.000 euros in cash, divided up and hidden inside cellophane bags.
The sequence described by the Carabinieri therefore includes following the wanted man on a public street, stopping him, and then carrying out a search of the premises of the residence. The rifle and money were found during the same capture operation, with the involvement of the Investigative Unit and the Calabria Airborne Squadron.
At the end of the required formalities, Dario De Bernardi was taken to Como Prison. The capture thus brought an end to the flight that began in 2011 and led to the man being held at the facility indicated by the Carabinieri after the operation in the province of Como.

### The vote on the Fortress
On 27 settembre, the citizens of Bellinzona will be called upon to express their views on Municipal Message 1019, dedicated to enhancing the UNESCO heritage of the Three Castles, the Murata and the city walls. The Municipal Council approved the message in marzo 2026. PLR Bellinzona invites voters to vote Yes.
The proposal concerns a complex that has been a World Heritage site for over twenty-five years. The PLR's position starts from this recognition and identifies the project as an opportunity to turn it into a driver of the City's development. The idea is to create a modern cultural and tourism offering capable of attracting visitors, extending their stay and generating benefits for businesses, restaurants, hotels and jobs throughout the region.
The project also concerns the museum offering. 35 years have passed since the last works, and the credit would make it possible to renovate and expand the exhibition spaces. Access to the Castles would be improved with the aim of making it easier and safer, bringing the visitor experience up to the standard of a site of global significance.
### A unique defensive system
The Fortress presents the Castles as a single defensive system, as recognized by UNESCO. The proposal also includes new spaces for events. According to the PLR, these spaces would benefit the population, which could continue to access the Castles.
The political message looks beyond an individual visit: according to the PLR, Bellinzona would have the opportunity to move from being a simple stopover to a true destination. The decision on 27 settembre therefore brings together heritage enhancement, museum renewal, accessibility, events and tourism promotion. The source also links the project to the local and regional economy, but the party's position remains above all an invitation to vote in favor of Message 1019. ## How much does the investment weigh on the City
The second profile to assess is economic. The PLR estimates an economic impact of more than 14 million francs and links it to support for small and medium-sized enterprises, described as the backbone of the City. In the framework described by the source, the project therefore does not remain confined to the spaces of the Castles: the effects indicated concern commerce, restaurants, hotel facilities and jobs throughout the region.
For cross-border commuters, the source does not indicate a specific effect. The concrete connection remains territorial and runs through the regional economic activities and jobs mentioned. The text speaks of an overall impact, without turning this indication into an individual figure or a number of hires. The sectors involved, however, remain clear: small and medium-sized enterprises, commerce, restaurants and hospitality.
The source distinguishes between the value of the investment and the portion directly supported by the City. A large part of the operation would be financed by the Canton, the Confederation and private parties. The share charged to Bellinzona is indicated as approximately 4.5 million francs. The PLR presents this participation as limited compared with the overall funding structure.

item.title: Swiss GDP 2026 revised upwards: +1.7% according to the KOF
item.description: KOF estimates GDP growth of 1.7% for 2026 (versus 0.9% in June) and inflation at 0.6%; euro at 0.93 francs in three months and 0.92 in one year.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Swiss GDP 2026 is estimated at +1,7% - In June, the GDP estimate was +0,9% - 2026 inflation is forecast at 0,6% - The euro is expected to be worth 0,93 francs in three months
## Key facts - Institute → KOF of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich - Edition → 123rd edition of the «Consensus Forecast» - Participants → 17 experts - Interviews → from 3 to 23 September - GDP 2026 → +1,7% excluding sports effects - Inflation 2026 → 0,6% - Euro/franc → 0,92 in one year - SPI → 20’633 points in twelve months
### GDP and prices change in the estimates
The forecasts for Switzerland's economic situation for the current year have improved significantly. The new survey by the KOF Institute of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich, conducted among the country's economists, indicates GDP growth of +1,7% for 2026, excluding sports effects. In June, the forecast was +0,9%.
The increase also concerns the following year: the current estimate is +1,7%, compared with +1,5% indicated in the June survey. However, the improvement in economic outlook expectations is accompanied by a downward revision of price forecasts.
For the current year, inflation is forecast at 0,6%, compared with 0,7% in June. For 2027, the forecast is 0,7%, compared with 0,8% previously; over a five-year horizon, it falls to 0,8%, whereas in June it was 0,9%.
The indications for the labor market remain almost unchanged. The unemployment rate is estimated at 3,1% in 2026, 3% in the following twelve months, a figure reported in the source as 3,0%, and 2,9% in five years.
The euro-franc exchange rate, which has risen over the past two months, is expected to remain broadly stable: 0,93 in three months and 0,92 in one year. For the dollar, the average values given are 0,81 and 0,80. For the cross-border commuter, [comparatore CHF/EUR](nav:exchange) is the currency reference closest to the cross-border dimension, without turning the forecast into a personal calculation.
The assessment of the stock market is more cautious: the SPI index is expected to reach around 19’725 points in one quarter, slightly below its current level, and 20’633 points in twelve months. This picture comes from the 123rd edition of the «Consensus Forecast», in which 17 experts interviewed between 3 and 23 September took part. The survey should not be confused with the forecasts of the KOF economic research center or its barometer. ## Exchange rate as a point of contact
### What can really be read
For a cross-border worker, the concrete link offered by the text is the euro-franc exchange rate. The source reports that the rate has increased over the past two months, but expects substantial stability over the coming horizons: 0,93 in three months and 0,92 in one year. The text does not announce any changes to rules, salaries or deductions.
In a scenario in which a cross-border worker receives income in francs and incurs expenses in euros, the two reference points can be used to observe the sensitivity of their budget in the short and medium term. However, the source does not provide the individual income, the frequency of exchanges, the timing of the conversion or the final result in euros. It is therefore not possible to derive a personal change in the payslip from the survey.
The revision of inflation should likewise be read as a general indicator. The change from 0,7% to 0,6% for the current year, from 0,8% to 0,7% in 2027 and from 0,9% to 0,8% over five years signals expectations of more contained price growth, not falling prices. There is no breakdown of expenses, territorial distinction or any amount relating to a family or a commuter.
The unemployment estimates likewise describe the labour market as a whole. They do not say whether an individual employment relationship will be renewed, modified or terminated. Dollar quotations and the SPI index remain further macroeconomic indicators, not direct measures of the income of a cross-border worker.
The survey does not discuss the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax or double taxation; nor does it propose a reading specific to Canton Ticino. For a separate comparison, [costo della vita Ticino vs Italia](nav:cost-of-living) may help organise the items to be observed, but it does not add data to the KOF survey.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## An operating procedure
### Five steps for using the data correctly
1. Set the horizon. Choose whether you are observing a near-term period, three months, or planning over twelve months or five years. The source uses these windows for exchange rates, prices, unemployment and the stock market. Do not mix a quarterly value with an annual one.
2. Separate the currencies. Create a row for the euro against the franc and note 0,93 at three months and 0,92 at one year. In a separate row, record the dollar, with average values of 0,81 and 0,80. The survey presents average forecasts: they are not personal quotes or guaranteed results.
3. Also record the comparison with June. For growth, place the +1,7% for 2026 alongside the previous +0,9% and the +1,7% for the following year alongside +1,5%. For inflation, keep the current and previous values separate. This makes the direction of the revisions visible without confusing different data.
4. Keep the indicators distinct. The unemployment rate concerns the labor market; the SPI concerns the stock market. For the latter, note 19’725 points in three months and 20’633 in twelve months, keeping the two horizons separate.
5. Verify the source. Indicate «Consensus Forecast», 123rd edition, 17 experts and interviews between 3 and 23 September. This information identifies the survey and helps avoid confusing it with the forecasts of the KOF economic research center or its barometer.
This outline allows the cross-border commuter to use the survey as a macroeconomic scenario, without attributing salary or contract data to it. For a personal simulation, open [calcolatore fiscale dello stipendio](nav:calculator).

item.title: Barco Saronno: cuts, strike and state of agitation
item.description: Fiom, Fim and Uilm declare industrial action at Barco in Saronno following the announcement of a reorganization. One hour of strike per shift, involving temporary agency workers and permanent employees.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - State of unrest at Barco in Saronno - One hour of strike per shift - Reorganization with impacts on three categories of workers - Second assembly scheduled for the afternoon
- Company: Barco di Saronno - Unions: Fiom Cgil, Fim Cisl dei Laghi, and Uilm Altomilanese - Production: operating room monitors - Reaction: state of unrest and one hour of strike per shift - Workers involved: agency workers, staff leasing, and permanent employees
In Saronno, Fiom Cgil, Fim Cisl dei Laghi, and Uilm Altomilanese have declared a state of unrest at Barco following the announcement of a production reorganization project. According to the information provided to the workers, the plan would have repercussions for agency workers, staff leasing personnel, and permanent employees.
Union representatives Otello Amabile (Uilm), Lorena Silvani (Fim), and Stefano Gallinaro (Fiom) met with employees in an assembly to explain the contents of the company communication. After half an hour of discussion, first-shift workers decided to proclaim a one-hour strike and open the state of unrest.
A second assembly is planned for the afternoon with second-shift workers. This meeting will also be accompanied by a second hour of strike. The mobilization therefore affects both shifts indicated in the source.
### Production and the unions' position
Barco is described as a Belgian metalworking multinational. At the Saronno site, it produces monitors for operating rooms, a sector in which the plant represents a production excellence.
The unions also pointed out the turnover of several people in company representation over the last few months. According to the organizations, the absence of an Italian management makes dialogue more complex.
Otello Amabile, from the Uilm Altomilanese secretariat, recalled that two years ago the executives had announced the purchase of land for a new hub. Subsequently, the company reportedly communicated that the project would not be realized and that a reorganization would be pursued instead. Amabile claims that «there is no loss of the Saronno site that justifies this reorganization» and links the concern to the repercussions on the entire factory.
The mobilization started immediately, with workers outside the gates, a state of unrest, and strikes for both shifts. The source does not mention new hires; to keep this dispute separate from the rest of the labor market, you can consult the [job advertisements](nav:jobs). ## The practical scope of the dispute
The most concrete data concerns the workforce indicated by the company and the unions: the reorganization would affect agency workers, staff leasing, and permanent staff. However, the source does not distinguish the effects for each category. It does not clarify which duties would be reorganized, how many workers would be involved, or what operational changes are planned.
### Communication, assessment, and consequences
To correctly understand the situation, three levels must be separated. The first is corporate communication: there is a project to reorganize production. The second is union assessment: the organizations request attention for the occupational consequences and consider the impact on the entire plant worrying. The third is the workers' reaction, which has chosen strike and state of agitation after the first‑shift assembly.
The source does not present a definitive outcome of the reorganization. It uses the conditional when speaking of repercussions and does not indicate closures, numbers of redundancies, or a already decided reduction of activity. For this reason the news documents a phase of negotiation and mobilization, not a final result.
Another element concerns expectations for the site. According to Amabile, two years ago the purchase of land for a new hub had been announced, but subsequently the company would have communicated that the project would not go ahead. The reorganization announced today is therefore also evaluated by the unions against that previous development prospect. The turnover of several people in the company representation and the absence of an Italian management further complicate the dialogue.
For a cross‑border reader from the Canton of Ticino, the scope is equally clear: the source does not mention G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax refunds, withholding tax, INPS, Brogeda, the new 2026 tax agreement, or double taxation. ### The stages indicated by the source
1. The company announces a production reorganization plan, presented to workers during the assemblies. 2. The representatives of Fiom, Fim and Uilm explain the company’s communication to the employees gathered in the assembly. 3. After half an hour of discussion, the first-shift workers decide on one hour of strike action and the opening of a state of unrest. 4. A second assembly with the second shift is scheduled for the afternoon, accompanied by a second hour of strike action.
This is the procedure reported in the source. No further deadlines, other assemblies, the number of positions affected or definitive decisions regarding the organization of the plant are indicated. Nor is it specified whether the consequences will be the same for agency workers, staff leasing workers and permanent employees.
To assess one’s position without adding elements not present in the report, the first reference is therefore the contractual category indicated in the communication and the shift involved in the assembly. Four high-end vehicles were stolen over the course of one week in Ticino, with thefts targeting dealers and body shops in Manno, Lamone and Camorino. The investigation launched after the incidents led to the arrest of three young men, while the search continues for a fourth suspect.

## In brief - Three nights of closures between A8 and D08 - Roadworks from 21:00 to 5:00 - Busto Arsizio, Besnate and Cavaria affected - Detours on state, provincial and municipal roads
## Key facts - What → vegetation maintenance work - Period → from lunedì 28 settembre to the early hours of giovedì 1 ottobre - Time → 21:00-5:00 - Operator → Autostrade per l’Italia - Infrastructure → A8 Milano-Varese and D08 - Reason → maintenance of tree vegetation
Starting lunedì 28 settembre, Autostrade per l’Italia has scheduled a series of overnight closures on the A8 Milano-Varese and the Gallarate-Gattico Branch, identified as D08. The works are concentrated between Busto Arsizio, Besnate and Cavaria and always take place from 21:00 to 5:00 the following morning. The schedule extends through the early hours of giovedì 1 ottobre. For a cross-border commuter, the information to verify is therefore the night on which the route passes through one of the affected sections: the source does not indicate border crossings or routes in Ticino, but describes the road network in the Varesotto area precisely.
### The schedule of the three interventions
The first closure is scheduled for the night between lunedì 28 and martedì 29 settembre. On D08, the section between the connection with the A8 and the Besnate exit, in the direction of the A26 Gravellona Toce, is closed. During the same period, the connecting ramp to D08 toward the A26 remains closed to those arriving from Varese on the A8.
Those who need to continue toward the A26 can exit at the Gallarate station on the A8, join the SS33 and continue along via dei Mille, via Bettolino and via Monte San Martino, then take the SP26 and re-enter D08 at the Besnate toll station. Alternatively, they can exit at Solbiate Arno-Albizzate and follow the SP26 and the SP49 to Besnate.
Between martedì 29 and mercoledì 30 settembre, the works move to the opposite carriageway of D08. The section between Besnate and the connection with the A8, in the direction of the Milano-Varese motorway, is closed. The Besnate station remains completely inaccessible for entry in either direction, A8 or A26. Vehicles heading toward the A8, after the mandatory exit at Besnate, must take the SP26, the SS33 del Sempione and the SS341 to the Gallarate toll station. Those who instead need to enter at Besnate toward the A26 can use the Vergiate station.
The final worksite, during the night between mercoledì 30 settembre and giovedì 1 ottobre, affects the A8 between Busto Arsizio and Cavaria in the direction of Varese. For those arriving from the A26 along D08, the connecting ramp to the A8 toward Varese is closed. The company managing the motorway network explained that the measures are needed «to allow tree maintenance work» along the affected sections. To correctly read the notice, the main criterion is to cross-reference the date, time slot and direction of travel. This is not a single repeated block: on the first night the critical point is the connection toward the A26; on the second, the direction toward the A8 and access to the Besnate station; on the third, the direction toward Varese on the A8 and the D08-A8 branch. For those who work in Ticino, the notice becomes relevant only if their route includes one of these sections.
### A different decision every night
This breakdown makes it possible to avoid a simple mistake: applying the diversion for the night of the 28th-29th to that of the 29th-30th. The directions also change for those departing from the same area. On the first night, there are two alternatives for the A26, using different exits, Gallarate or Solbiate Arno-Albizzate. On the second, by contrast, access to Besnate is closed in both directions, and the source separates the flow heading directly toward the A8 from that which must enter toward the A26. The reference point indicated for the latter is Vergiate.
The last night also requires a distinction. Those heading toward Varese must exit at Busto Arsizio and use the SS336, SS33 and SS341 before re-entering the A8 at the Cavaria or Solbiate Arno-Albizzate junctions. Those who must continue toward Gravellona from the D08, on the other hand, follow the secondary road network, with SS336, SS33, SP26 and SP49, to re-enter the D08 at Besnate. The two routes start from the same closure, but have different destinations.
The fact that the closures are scheduled between 21:00 and 5:00 limits the analysis to that window. The source does not report daytime closures, so the measure cannot automatically be extended to the entire day. For a commuter, the practical choice depends on the actual time of passage: if it coincides with the indicated time slot, the diversion planned for that night is needed; if it falls outside the time slot, the notice does not describe a closure.
The text does not quantify travel times, queues or delays, nor does it indicate effects on border crossings, traffic in Ticino or alternative services. 2. Determine the direction. Establishing whether the journey is toward the A26, toward the A8 Milano-Varese, or toward Varese makes it possible to match the route to the correct detour.
3. For the night of 28-29, if the destination is the A26, before the closed entrance choose either the Gallarate exit, via SS33, via dei Mille, via Bettolino, via Monte San Martino and SP26 to Besnate, or the Solbiate Arno-Albizzate exit, following SP26 and SP49.

item.title: Trenord leaves 30 passengers stranded in Gallarate, Region must intervene
item.description: During the night between September 22 and 23, around thirty passengers bound for Malpensa were left stranded at Gallarate after the departure of the last empty train, without assistance or connections.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Around thirty passengers were left at Gallarate - The incident occurred between 22 and 23 September - The travelers were headed to Malpensa - Astuti asks the Region for clarification
- Location → Gallarate station - When → night between 22 and 23 September - Passengers involved → around thirty - Destination → Malpensa - Problem reported → no connection or assistance - Political request → clarification and checks by the Region
### The night between 22 and 23 September
During the night between 22 and 23 September, around thirty travelers were left at Gallarate station after the departure of the last train. The passengers were supposed to travel to Malpensa, but were left stranded without connections or assistance.
The account reported in the source presents a decisive detail: the last train departed regularly, but without anyone on board. The group therefore found itself without an available connection and, according to reports, without communication or support from the company.
The case was brought back into the spotlight by Pd regional councillor Samuele Astuti, after he read the first-person testimony of a passenger involved in the misadventure.
The political objection is summed up in the sentence: «Trenord abandoned around thirty passengers at Gallarate; the Region should demand answers from the company».
For Astuti, if the events happened as described, this is not a simple service disruption. The councillor stressed that thirty people cannot be left at midnight, in a closed station, without a connection and without assistance. The request is directed at the Lombardy Region, which should also clarify why assistance was not provided to the passengers.
According to the councillor, the incident comes less than a week after the report of disruptions and cancellations on the Varesotto lines. Astuti called the new incident even more outrageous and linked the matter to another objection: while service disruptions increase, fares are also rising.
The next step is political. Next month, the Regional Council will discuss the Regional Mobility and Transport Program; on that occasion, the Pd group intends to ask that quality, reliability and passenger assistance be concrete objectives. The position expressed is that it is unacceptable to pay more for a service in which, in cases like this, even basic assistance is lacking. ### The issue is not only the delay
The matter, viewed from a practical standpoint, is not described as a simple delayed train. What is being challenged is the overall sequence: the travelers had to reach Malpensa, the last train departed as scheduled, but the group was left behind and without assistance. According to Astuti, it is this combination that takes the case beyond an ordinary service disruption.
For those who need to reach Malpensa, the difference between a canceled service and a train that departs without passengers is not explained by the source in terms of schedules or alternatives. The text does not indicate whether other connections were available, what communications were given before departure, or what solution was proposed to the people left at the station. These details cannot be added to the reconstruction.
The central question therefore becomes procedural. Regione Lombardia is called upon to ask Trenord which procedures were activated and why assistance was not provided. No response from the company or Regione Lombardia is reported, however. The reader can thus distinguish between the fact recounted and the checks still requested: the former is the group’s remaining without a connection or support; the latter concern operational responsibilities and methods of assistance.
For the Frontaliere Ticino audience, the thematic boundary must be kept clear: the source does not mention permesso G, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, or double taxation. It therefore provides no information on these matters, nor does it authorize connecting the episode to topics other than the transport incident in the Varesotto area.
The reference to fares, too, should be read as Astuti’s political statement. The source reports that, in his view, service disruptions and fares are increasing together; it does not provide amounts, percentages, dates of increases, or a fare comparison. For this reason, it is not possible to turn that statement into a calculation of the cost of the journey.
As a separate in-depth resource on mobility services, the reader can consult [mezzi pubblici Ticino](nav:transport), without attributing information about the Gallarate case to that page.

item.title: Roberto Gatti and Sons of a Minor Goal: 11 Promotions
item.description: The former footballer and coach from Varese recounts the eleven promotions between Chiasso, Lugano and Solbiatese in the VareseNews podcast.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Roberto Gatti grew up at Varese, between the pitch and the bench - From Switzerland to Italy: eleven promotions - First promotion as a coach: Chiasso - Solbiatese victorious in the Eccellenza playoffs
## Key facts - Protagonist → Roberto Gatti - First steps as a footballer → Barcanova - Arrival at Varese → early '80s - First promotion as a coach → Chiasso - Promotions → eleven
Roberto Gatti built a career between Italy and Switzerland, first as a player and then as a coach, with Varese becoming his sporting home and Chiasso at the center of his first promotion from the bench. The new episode of «Figli di un gol minore» retraces this journey, from his origins beneath the Mole to the eleven promotions won on pitches in the two countries.
### From the Mole to Varese
Raised in the shadow of Grande Torino, with his father passing on his passion to him, Gatti took his first steps at Barcanova. In the early '80s, he arrived at Varese and found his place beneath Sacro Monte. His debut, at a very young age, came in Serie B, under the guidance of Catuzzi, described in the source as an innovator. Beppe Marotta also worked at that Varese, at the time a promising executive.
As a player, Gatti developed a precise tactical identity. He was a defender of another era, committed to pure man-marking, but he was also among the first to experiment with the early theories of zonal play. His personal ties to the Varese area and the club's subsequent bankruptcy took him across the border. In Switzerland, he wore the shirts of Lugano and Chiasso, collected promotions and experienced high-level football across the Alps, alongside numerous Swiss internationals.
His move to the bench came almost by chance, precisely at Chiasso. At just thirty, he took charge of the first team and secured his first historic promotion to Serie B. It was from that moment that the reputation of «Mister Promozione» took shape: a pragmatic and charismatic coach, capable of achieving eleven promotions between Switzerland and Italy. The clubs he led include Mozzate, Inveruno, Sant'Angelo and Solbiate, along with Solbiatese's recent triumph in the Eccellenza playoffs. ## The journey that earns a nickname
The reputation of «Mr. Promotion» takes shape after his move from Chiasso and his numerous experiences in Switzerland and Italy. The source describes him as a pragmatic and charismatic coach, capable of achieving as many as eleven promotions. The towns of Mozzate, Inveruno, Sant'Angelo and Solbiate are part of the same trajectory.
His approach is based on managing large squads and on the quality of individual players. These are the elements through which Roberto Gatti is presented as a provincial leader, capable of leaving an indelible mark in every dressing room. The profile is not limited to results: it also encompasses the way he leads large squads and brings out the quality of individual players.
### Two snapshots of the journey
Among the most iconic moments is the dramatic survival secured in the Serie D relegation playoffs with Sant'Angelo. Survival was decided in the 91st minute by a memorable bicycle kick, an episode cited among the most significant of Gatti's journey.
The other highlighted passage is more recent and concerns Solbiatese, the protagonist of a triumph in the Eccellenza playoffs. The result is part of the journey of the eleven triumphs built by the coach between the two countries, following experiences gained in towns such as Mozzate, Inveruno, Sant'Angelo and Solbiate.
The account thus juxtaposes survival secured in stoppage time and a triumph achieved in the playoffs. These are two episodes evoked to describe the journey of a coach who has built his reputation in provincial football, through the management of large squads, the quality of individual players and the ability to leave a mark in dressing rooms. ## From address book to podcast
For a decade, «Sons of a minor goal» was a column in VareseNews dedicated to the most beautiful and fascinating stories of amateur football. Its evolution was born with Radio Materia, the VareseNews website: today the project is also a podcast with the voices of the protagonists.
The audio format includes interviews with the interpreters of "bread and salami" football. The storytelling field includes the great former players loaned to the lower categories, the great-small businesses born on the provincial fields and the adventures lived around the world, including in Vanuatu.
The episode dedicated to Roberto Gatti is part of this series of stories. Its history, between Varese, Chiasso, Lugano and the other squares led on the bench, represents for the same source a perfect example of what it means to be "Children of a minor goal". The podcast thus brings the voice of the protagonists to the fore, according to the formula announced with the birth of Radio Materia.
The new episode can be heard every day at 12 noon on Radio Materia and on all audio streaming platforms. The daily appointment accompanies the passage of the column from the written story to the series of interviews, keeping the stories of amateur football and the people who have lived them at the centre. The story of Gatti enters this path as one of the stories related to the eleven promotions between Switzerland and Italy.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 22 settembre 2026: Report no. 27 published - Projected retirement age of 67 years and 6 months in 2030 - Pension spending at 17,1% of GDP in 2041 - The document does not change the current rules
## Key facts Document → Report no. 27 Publication → 22 settembre 2026 Author → Ragioneria Generale dello Stato Projection 2030 → 67 years and 6 months Projection 2040 → 68 years and 2 months Projection 2050 → 70 years Pension spending → 17,1% of GDP in 2041
On 22 settembre 2026, Ragioneria Generale dello Stato published Report no. 27 on the future trend of spending on pensions, healthcare, and elderly care. The document shows what will happen, in economic terms, if the current rules remain unchanged.
The passage of greatest interest to those following pension eligibility requirements concerns the access age. After the requirements already set for 2027 and 2028, the projections increase the age in line with life expectancy: 67 years and 6 months in 2030, 68 years and 2 months in 2040, and 70 years in 2050. Ragioneria thus highlights the need for an increase in the retirement age.
### Projections and current rules
The report does not introduce new rules. This clarification separates the forward-looking data from the rules currently in force: 2030 is indicated as a projection, while the requirements for 2027 and 2028 are described as already set. The document therefore offers an economic view of the future, not a new procedure for applying for a pension.
Pension spending is projected at 17,1% of GDP in 2041. This percentage is part of the overall spending analysis and does not indicate the retirement age of an individual worker.
The scope of the Report is broader than just the timetable: it includes pensions, healthcare, and elderly care. The GDP figure should therefore be read within the assessment of the future trend of these items, while the ages indicated describe the projected evolution of the requirements in line with life expectancy.
As for current requirements, the text refers to the situation concerning the age and requirements for retiring in 2026. It also refers to the latest INPS instructions on pensions for 2027-2028.

### Three Reading Steps
1. Separate rules from forecasts. Note in two lines the requirements already set and, separately, the projections linked to life expectancy. Do not mix the two frameworks. 2. Check the time reference. For the near term, the text refers to the situation regarding age and the requirements for retiring in 2026 and the latest INPS instructions on pensions for 2027-2028. 3. Keep the in-depth material separate. item.title: At Pasture, the operator changes: jobs at risk
item.description: Starting in January, the federal mandate for the asylum center will pass from AOZ to ORS: in Ticino, 120 employees are currently working, but not all of them will be rehired.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The federal mandate will pass from AOZ to ORS in January - ORS will not rehire all employees currently in service - In Ticino, there are currently 120 employees in service
## Key facts - What: change of operator for assistance - Where: Pasture - When: in January - Current operator: AOZ - New operator: ORS - Personnel indicated for Ticino: 120 employees - Announced outcome: not all will be rehired
At Pasture, the federal mandate for the asylum centre will pass from AOZ to ORS in January. The news brings together two elements: the change of operator for assistance and the possible effect on staffing. ORS, in fact, will not rehire all employees currently in service.
The available data concerns Ticino: today there are 120 employees in service. The source does not specify how many work at Pasture, how many are employed in assisting the asylum centre and how many will be rehired by the new operator. For this reason, the precise number of jobs at risk is not indicated. The title points to employment risk, but the text does not allow it to be converted into a figure.
### What changes in January
Before the changeover, the federal mandate for the asylum centre is entrusted to AOZ; from January it will pass to ORS. The sequence is clear, while the exact date of the change, the reasons for the replacement and the criteria by which ORS will determine which employees to rehire are not included in the news. Nor are any individual communications, contractual conditions or timelines for personnel indicated.
For those who work in the assistance sector at Pasture, the concrete issue is therefore continuity with the new operator. The source confirms that it will not concern all employees currently in service, but does not say how many will remain, how many will leave or whether the overall number will change in a clearly defined way.
### The figure not to confuse
The 120 employees mentioned is the figure referring to Ticino today. They are not presented as the number of positions available at ORS and are not described as the number of people who will lose their jobs. This distinction is essential for reading the news correctly and for not attributing to the source information that it does not contain.
The possible connection with cross-border work is limited: the decision concerns employment in Ticino. The source, however, does not indicate how many cross-border commuters are among the 120 employees or whether the change involves people with a G permit. Any individual assessment therefore remains tied to information about the individual employment relationship, which is not detailed in the article. Per chi lavora nel Canton Ticino, il passaggio ha una conseguenza pratica precisa: il riferimento operativo indicato dalla notizia cambia da AOZ a ORS, ma la continuità non è garantita per l'intero personale. Non è però possibile leggere il cambio come una modifica generale del mercato del lavoro o come una nuova regola per tutti i lavoratori. La fonte riguarda il mandato federale per il Centro d'asilo di Pasture e i dipendenti oggi in servizio in Ticino.
### Prima e dopo
| Prima | Dopo | |---|---| | Operatore indicato: AOZ | Operatore indicato: ORS | | Mandato federale presso AOZ | Passaggio del mandato a gennaio | | Dipendenti in servizio in Ticino | 120 oggi, ma ORS non riassumerà tutti |
Il confronto aiuta a separare ciò che è già definito da ciò che non lo è. Prima, AOZ è l'operatore collegato al mandato. Dopo, ORS subentra a gennaio e non riassume tutti i dipendenti in servizio. La notizia non dice se il personale escluso sarà sostituito, se il servizio avrà una dimensione diversa o se ci saranno altre posizioni. Non si possono quindi costruire scenari numerici.
Per un frontaliere che lavorasse nell'attività interessata, il punto sarebbe verificare se il proprio posto rientra tra quelli riassunti. Ma il testo non pubblica un elenco, non distingue tra residenti e frontalieri e non indica quanti dei 120 siano lavoratori italiani. Il totale del Ticino non può essere trasformato in una stima dell'impatto sulla mobilità transfrontaliera.
Il perimetro informativo è altrettanto importante. Nel testo non compaiono riferimenti a [permesso G/B](nav:permits), AVS, LPP, LAMal, [ristorni Ticino-Italia](nav:ristorni) o imposta alla fonte. Per questo la notizia non consente di ricavare scadenze, diritti, trattenute o procedure su questi temi. Sono elementi estranei al contenuto disponibile, non spiegazioni del cambio di operatore.
### Nessun calcolo automatico dei posti
Quando l'articolo dice che non tutti saranno riassunti, comunica una riduzione rispetto all'intero gruppo, ma non una percentuale. L'unico numero certo resta 120, riferito ai dipendenti in Ticino oggi; manca il dato sulla sede di Pasture e manca il numero dei riassunti. Anche per un frontaliere, quindi, non è corretto dedurre un rischio individuale dal solo fatto che il mandato cambi. La fonte non afferma che ORS stia assumendo e non indica posizioni alternative.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). For those directly concerned, the possible action is above all an orderly verification of the information, without attributing to the text documents or deadlines it does not contain.
### Four possible checks
1. Delimit the case. The news concerns the federal mandate for the Pasture Asylum Center. Working in Ticino, by itself, is not enough to say that one’s position is affected.
2. Compare the two operators. AOZ is the name linked to the mandate before the change; ORS is the new operator indicated for January. The month is the only time reference provided.
3. Separate the general data from the personal data. The 120 employees refer to Ticino today. They are not 120 positions declared at risk, nor are they the number of employees ORS will rehire.
4. Verify the reabsorption. The source makes clear that ORS will not take on all the employees, but it does not say who will be rehired, within what timeframe, or according to which criteria. Without these elements, it is not possible to complete the verification of the individual case.
This procedure does not replace individual communication; it serves to avoid confusing the change of operator with an already quantified dismissal. The text does not indicate offices, forms, documents, contacts, number of positions, the exact date in January, or contractual conditions. Consequently, it is not possible to invent administrative steps or indicate an application to submit.
For the cross-border reader, the same caution applies to topics that are not in the news. Possession of a G permit, calculation of withholding tax, AVS, LPP, or LAMal are not linked to the change. The source does not even say whether the worker concerned lives across the border. Any further investigation into these instruments must remain separate from the Pasture report.
If the goal is to monitor possible alternatives, the [annunci di lavoro](nav:jobs) can be consulted, without presenting results not cited as ORS offers. If, instead, one wants to estimate the economic effect of a personal scenario, the news provides no information on salary, working hours, allowances, or deductions. To compare possible income scenarios, use [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator).

item.title: Reduce recovery times after the A2 Mezzovico incident
item.description: Lorenzo Quadri (Lega) presents a motion to reduce restoration times after the accident on the A2 in Mezzovico: closure lasting over 5 hours, queues up to 13 km.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Lorenzo Quadri calls for faster response times after accidents - In Mezzovico, the A2 remained closed for more than five hours - The queues reached 13 kilometres - The motion proposes coordination and the use of drones
## Key facts - Request → significantly reduce restoration times - Proposer → Lorenzo Quadri, Lega dei Ticinesi - Location → A2 at Mezzovico - Direction → northbound - Reopening → full reopening more than five hours after the accident - Queues → up to 13 kilometres - Responsibility → Confederation and Ustra - Action → motion to the Federal Council
Lorenzo Quadri, National Councillor of Lega dei Ticinesi, presented a motion to the Federal Council to significantly reduce the time required to restore motorway traffic after accidents. The request stems from an incident on the A2 in Mezzovico: northbound traffic remained blocked, and full reopening came more than five hours after the accident.
The source reports two dates: 5 August in the standfirst and 8 August in the passage reproducing the motion. The text nevertheless highlights the same operational elements: blocked traffic, full reopening more than five hours later, and queues of up to 13 kilometres. In the motion submitted in Bern, Quadri describes some timeframes as “really difficult to justify.”
### The problem identified in the motion
The source does not directly mention cross-border workers. For people in this situation, the practical connection exists only when their own route coincides with the road network concerned. The source does not quantify how many workers were involved, indicate an alternative schedule, or propose a replacement route. It does, however, describe the consequences that, according to the motion, situations of this kind can cause: inconvenience to users, lost work hours, delays in transporting people and goods, higher consumption, and repercussions on the secondary road network.
The source presents a request to the Federal Council, not the announcement of a procedure already in force. It calls for the timeframes to be reviewed and, where necessary, for the way operations are organized to be reconsidered. The management of national roads, the text specifies, falls within the remit of the Confederation and Ustra, the Federal Roads Office.
The requested review does not concern a single entity. Quadri points to coordination between Ustra, cantonal authorities, the police, emergency services and companies tasked with vehicle recovery. The political objective is to reduce the time required to restore normal traffic conditions, without separating this need from rescue, safety and fact-finding activities. These elements define the scope of the motion; the source does not attribute the duration of the closure to a specific body and does not announce a decision by the Federal Council. ## The practical point for those who commute
### From full reopening to partial reopening
The proposal does not indicate a new route to avoid the A2. It asks for the phase following an accident to be measured differently: the Federal Council should verify target times for at least a partial reopening of the carriageway. The condition is precise: the necessary rescue operations, safety measures and investigations must be guaranteed.
For the cross-border commuter facing a closure, the distinction puts the moment when part of the carriageway could become available again in the foreground, even without a full reopening. However, this is the implication of the request, not an announced service. The motion does not set out minutes, indicate a lane or guarantee passage. Based on the source, it does not change the situation of anyone who has to cross the section.
The value of the proposal lies in connecting two requirements that the text holds together: significantly reducing restoration times and maintaining the necessary investigations. A cross-border commuter can use this distinction to read any future communications: a partial reopening is not equivalent to a full one, and neither is taken for granted by the motion.
### The chain of responsibilities
The second aspect is organizational. Quadri asks for procedures and coordination between Ustra, cantonal authorities, the police, rescue services and companies tasked with vehicle recovery to be reviewed and, if necessary, revised. The source does not say which group determined the duration of the closure at Mezzovico: the case cannot become an accusation against a single party.
The request for an intercantonal comparison opens another perspective. The motion proposes comparing motorway closure and reopening times after similar accidents, looking for differences in the procedures and intervention methods of the various Cantons. No ranking, results or better procedure are provided. For the cross-border commuter, the comparison would make sense only as a basis for understanding any differences, once the requested elements are available.
Technology is the final piece. The motion calls for examining a more extensive use of technological means to collect and secure evidence, citing surveys conducted via drones. The source does not announce drones already being used on the A2 and does not link their use to a precise time. It presents them as a possibility to be examined, within a management approach that must keep surveys and restoration together. Anyone following the effect of closures on their own route can consult the [storico traffico/code ai valichi](nav:traffic-history), keeping mobility data separate from the parliamentary request.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ## How to read the proposal without confusing it with a decision
### Commuter checklist
The source presents a parliamentary act and the measures requested, not an individual procedure for the user. For a cross-border commuter, the concrete action compatible with the available data is therefore an orderly review: distinguish the episode cited, the requests addressed to the Federal Council, and what might eventually be decided afterward. The following sequence only restates the elements present in the motion.
1. Identify the stretch. If one's journey concerns the A2 at Mezzovico northbound, the reference is the blockage described in the source. One can note the full reopening more than five hours after the accident and queues extending up to 13 kilometres. No times or routes not indicated by the text should be added. 2. Separate the phases. The request for target times concerns at least a partial reopening after rescue operations, safety and the necessary investigations have been ensured. These requirements are the conditions explicitly set out in the act. 3. Identify the parties. The scope indicated includes the Confederation and Ustra, cantonal authorities, police, emergency services and companies tasked with recovering vehicles. The source does not assign the cross-border commuter an application to submit to any of these bodies. 4. Check the comparison. The act calls for an intercantonal comparison of closure and reopening times after similar accidents. The text provided contains no results, rankings or differences already measured. The information to look for, if it is produced, is therefore the requested comparison, not an advance conclusion. 5. Distinguish the technology. Drones are cited as a notable example for collecting and securing evidence. The source mentions their use as a possibility to examine, but does not report their use in the Mezzovico case. To monitor their own route, the cross-border commuter can supplement reading the news report with consulting [storico traffico/code ai valichi](nav:traffic-history), without considering the tool an official communication about the A2.
This procedure also helps read the economic consequences without inflating them. The motion lists lost working hours, delays in the transport of people and goods, higher consumption and repercussions on the secondary road network. However, it does not assign an amount to an individual user and does not quantify the cost of a traffic queue. For a cross-border commuter, those four elements are categories of impact described by the source, not rights or figures already recognized.
To monitor traffic using a tool consistent with the subject, consult [storico traffico/code ai valichi](nav:traffic-history).

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Ffs Cargo reorganization: 80 employees involved - Government, Ferrovie and trade unions take stock - Three employees without job offers
## Key facts - What → reorganization of Ffs Cargo - Employees involved → 80 - Open situation → 3 employees without offers - Parties involved → Government, Ferrovie management and trade union organizations
## The discussion on the reorganization
Ffs Cargo is at the center of a discussion about employment prospects. Government, Ferrovie management and trade union organizations took stock of the reorganization affecting eighty employees. The still-open situation concerns three employees, who have no job offers.
The gist of the news is all here: on the one hand, there is a reorganization process involving 80 people; on the other, there are three positions for which, in the picture reported by the source, no proposal has yet been indicated. The text adds no names, roles, workplaces or details of any possible solutions.
### The discussion among the three parties
The news places Government, Ferrovie management and trade union organizations on the same footing as the parties taking stock. However, it does not attribute individual statements, indicate which organization took a position or report a concluding agreement. For this reason, the verb discuss contained in the title describes a discussion about employment prospects, while the figure regarding the three employees signals that at least part of the reorganization remains open.
The reference to Ffs Cargo identifies the company concerned. The available text does not go into the activities affected by the reorganization and does not explain whether the job offers concern transfers, new duties or other arrangements. Nor does it indicate the schedule of the discussion, upcoming deadlines or the place where the review took place.
### What is confirmed
The company involved, the reorganization, the total number of employees affected and the number of employees still without an offer are confirmed. It is not possible, however, to derive from the source a ranking of the positions, a geographical distribution or a definitive outcome. The phrase employment prospects also remains general: it signals the employment issue but does not describe conditions, amounts or timing.
For readers following the case in Canton Ticino, the news therefore provides a limited snapshot. The discussion is ongoing, the parties are identified and three situations still have no job offer; beyond these elements, the text offers no details. Those who want to follow the employment issue can supplement their reading with [annunci di lavoro](nav:jobs), without confusing the general catalog with the specific data concerning Ffs Cargo. ## What it means for those who work across the border
For a cross-border worker employed by Ffs Cargo, the source does not describe a change already defined in terms of pay, leave or social security. Instead, it describes a reorganization affecting 80 employees and leaving three staff members without job offers. The source does not say whether any cross-border workers are among these employees: any personal connection therefore remains to be verified.
### A clear boundary between fact and hypothesis
The report is presented in the Canton Ticino section, but this does not make it possible to reconstruct the situation of every commuter. The text does not indicate the employees' duties, workplace, contract, length of service or place of residence. It therefore does not make it possible to say who is destined for a change of activity, who has received an offer or whether a proposal entails a concrete change in the daily commute.
For those who cross the border, this distinction matters. The source does not mention G permits, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax, INPS, Brogeda or double taxation. Nor does it contain any references to the new 2026 tax agreement. These issues cannot automatically be linked to the reorganization solely on the basis of the news. The verifiable fact remains employment-related: Ffs Cargo, 80 employees involved, three staff members still without an offer.
| Question for the worker | What the source allows one to say | | --- | --- | | Is the position within the scope of the reorganization? | The text indicates 80 employees involved, but does not list the names. | | Is there already a proposal? | The source reports three staff members still without an offer, without indicating the other cases. | | Are the route or conditions changing? | Workplace, duties, hours, amounts or conditions are not reported. |
### The practical reading
The news does not authorize turning a collective fact into an individual outcome. A cross-border worker who recognizes themselves as falling within the company scope may consider the reorganization a matter to follow, but cannot derive from the source a transfer date, a dismissal, a new salary or a tax impact. For the other workers, the text does not make it possible to know what proposal was made.
The practical value of the article therefore lies in mapping the open questions. The discussion among the Government, Railways and trade unions concerns work; the position of three staff members remains without an offer; everything else requires further communication. For a broader reading of the market, the site also offers [aziende che assumono](nav:companies), but that path does not replace the missing data on the reorganization.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ## Come verificare la propria situazione
Per chi vuole usare la notizia in modo operativo, il percorso deve restare aderente ai pochi dati disponibili. Nel testo non compaiono una procedura aziendale, una scadenza o un documento da consegnare. Si può però ordinare la verifica in passaggi, senza attribuire alla riorganizzazione effetti che la fonte non descrive.
### 1. Separare il dato collettivo dal caso personale
Il primo passaggio è riconoscere il perimetro: la riorganizzazione di Ffs Cargo tocca 80 dipendenti. Questo numero non identifica il singolo lavoratore e non dice se la sua posizione rientri tra le tre ancora senza proposte. Per un frontaliere, quindi, la domanda iniziale non è fiscale: è capire se il proprio rapporto di lavoro è compreso nella riorganizzazione richiamata dalla notizia.
### 2. Verificare quale situazione è già definita
Il secondo passaggio consiste nel distinguere tra una proposta lavorativa e l'assenza di proposta. La fonte afferma soltanto che tre collaboratori sono ancora senza proposte; non descrive il contenuto delle altre soluzioni e non fornisce un termine entro cui riceverle. Non si possono aggiungere mansioni, sedi, salari, orari o date. Se il lavoratore non appartiene al gruppo dei tre, la fonte non consente comunque di sapere quale proposta lo riguardi.
### 3. Tenere separati lavoro e temi di frontiera
Il terzo passaggio è non usare questo articolo come risposta a questioni che non contiene. Permesso G, AVS, LPP, LAMal, imposta alla fonte, INPS, ristorni, Brogeda, doppia imposizione e nuovo accordo fiscale 2026 non sono trattati nel testo. La notizia non dà istruzioni su documenti, valichi, previdenza o tasse. Per il frontaliere, questo evita di leggere come cambiamento fiscale una notizia che riguarda soltanto, nei dati disponibili, una riorganizzazione occupazionale.
### 4. Seguire gli interlocutori indicati
L'ultimo punto da monitorare riguarda i soggetti citati: Governo, direzione delle Ferrovie e sigle sindacali. Sono gli interlocutori che, secondo la fonte, hanno fatto il punto. Il testo non indica un canale, una data o un esito successivo; perciò non si può costruire una scadenza. Quando serviranno numeri individuali, contenuti delle proposte o effetti sul rapporto di lavoro, questi elementi dovranno arrivare da una comunicazione specifica.
Per una simulazione separata della busta paga, puoi usare il [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator).

Per il frontaliere, il comunicato va letto distinguendo la decisione già presa dall’eventualità lasciata aperta. La decisione è il mantenimento del tasso di riferimento; l’eventualità è un possibile intervento sul mercato dei cambi, subordinato alla necessità di garantire condizioni monetarie adeguate. La fonte non comunica un intervento già eseguito, né offre un valore del franco rispetto a una valuta specifica.
### Il cambio resta un indicatore, non una nuova regola
Questo limita anche le conclusioni sulla vita quotidiana. Un eventuale movimento del cambio può rendere diversa la conversione del denaro per chi attraversa il confine, ma il testo non dice in quale direzione si muoverà il franco e non quantifica vantaggi o costi. Per questo il [comparatore CHF/EUR](nav:exchange) può servire a osservare il dato corrente, mentre la notizia BNS serve a capire quali fattori la banca centrale considera. Non bisogna trasformare la disponibilità a intervenire in una previsione certa.
| Segnale della BNS | Lettura prudente | |---|---| | Tasso invariato | Nessuna nuova decisione sul tasso di riferimento | | Disponibilità sul mercato dei cambi | Possibilità condizionata, non intervento annunciato | | Petrolio e inflazione | Pressione indicata dalla fonte, senza stima sul bilancio individuale | | PIL rivisto al rialzo | Previsione macroeconomica, non promessa su salari o occupazione |
Il perimetro della notizia resta monetario. Il testo non tratta il permesso G, AVS, LPP, LAMal, i ristorni, l’imposta alla fonte, INPS, Brogeda, il Canton Ticino o la doppia imposizione. Non offre quindi elementi per descrivere un nuovo accordo fiscale 2026, né per modificare procedure fiscali, previdenziali o di frontiera sulla base di questa sola decisione.
L’aggiornamento del PIL può essere letto come una valutazione più favorevole sull’economia svizzera per il 2026, ma la fonte non collega quella revisione a nuove assunzioni, a salari più alti o a cambiamenti nel mercato del lavoro dei frontalieri. Allo stesso modo, l’inflazione legata al petrolio spiega la revisione delle proiezioni, ma non determina da sola il costo concreto di ogni famiglia. Chi vive tra Svizzera e Italia può quindi usare il comunicato come segnale da seguire, mantenendo separati i dati ufficiali dalle ipotesi personali. For those considering moving from Gornate Olona, disposable income does not coincide solely with the amount of employment income. Correct reading passes through the pension and insurance items that affect net pay, while housing choice requires a separate comparison with commuting and daily expenses.
### Items to read before net
| Item | Data indicated by the source | |---|---| | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% for the employee | | AD/AC | 1.1%; cap CHF 148'200 | | LAINF | 0.7–1.5% | | LPP | 7–18% by age bracket, from age 25 |
The age data matters for LPP, because the source indicates a percentage ranging from 7% to 18% by age bracket starting at age 25. For AVS/AI/IPG the indicated reference is instead 5.3% borne by the employee. AD/AC equals 1.1% with a limit of CHF 148'200, while LAINF ranges from 0.7% to 1.5%. These items should be read together, not replaced with a single percentage.
Alongside pensions there is LAMal, i.e., health insurance. Cross‑border workers with a G permit have the option right, and the adult franchises indicated in the source range from CHF 300 to CHF 2'500. This is a distinct choice from the withholding tax, but it enters monthly spending planning and should be considered when comparing housing alternatives.
### Italian tax: comparison without double withholding
For 2026 the source indicates Italian IRPEF rates of 23% up to €28'000, 33% between €28'001 and €50'000, and 43% above €50'000, based on Law 199/2025, article 1, paragraph 3. For 2024–2025 incomes the indicated rates are 23%, 35% and 43%. These values do not cancel the rule of withholding only in Switzerland and the tax credit in the CE box of the 730.
Switzerland does not belong to the EU or the EEA, so it is not advisable to automatically assimilate its system to the Italian or European one. For the housing part, without verified values one should not assign standard travel times, links or costs to Gornate Olona. item.title: Luino-Switzerland line: Action adheres to Lombardy moves
item.description: Saturday, September 26, mobilization in the Lombard stations for railway efficiency. Focus on the Luino-Switzerland route and collection of signatures for the Minister.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Azione joins the 'Lombardia si muove' protest - Mobilization is scheduled for Saturday, September 26 - Focus on the Luino-Switzerland line - Signature collection regarding the status of works
## Key Facts - When → Saturday, September 26 - Participants → Azione, commuters' committees, and political representatives - Location → Lombardy stations - Investment → approximately 120 million euros - Section → approximately 15 kilometers on Italian territory - S30 Frequency → from two per hour to 4 daily trips - Speed → 30 km/h - Stations → Luino and Maccagno
On Saturday, September 26, Azione will join the 'Lombardia si muove' protest, a cross-party and itinerant initiative bringing together commuters' committees and political representatives across Lombardy's stations. The demand is clear: greater efficiency in rail connections, just as work and school activities resume after the summer and commuters once again face chronic delays, cancelled trains, and prolonged waits.
For those departing from the north of the Varese province to reach Switzerland for work, the mobilization highlights a strategic section for the connection with Swiss territory. Azione considers the line between Luino and Switzerland, part of the Alptransit and Rhine-Alpine corridors, to be strategic yet neglected. Alongside the presence at the stations, the initiative includes a signature collection to demand an account of the progress of the works directly from the Minister of Transport.
### The Luino-Magadino Connection
The press release refers to the international agreement between the two countries, under which Switzerland funded the redevelopment of the Luino-Magadino line with approximately 120 million euros. This involves about 15 kilometers on Italian territory, intended for both freight and passenger traffic. This economic figure is contrasted with the current operational conditions denounced by Azione.
The press release summarizes the contrast with one phrase:
> «Despite this massive investment, the situation on the ground is paradoxical».
The S30 suburban trains between Luino and Cadenzazzo, described as useful for short distances and strategic for accessing Gotthard passenger services, have gone from two per hour to just four daily trips. The Italian section, the press release adds, is traveled at 30 kilometers per hour.
The indicated consequences directly affect commuters from Pino, Maccagno, Colmegna, and Luino. Those traveling for work must resort to alternative means to find reliable connections to Milan or Switzerland, thereby increasing the isolation of mountain areas. Furthermore, at the Luino and Maccagno stations, out-of-order elevators, broken information displays, a lack of platform shelters, broken glass, and insufficient, obsolete, damaged, or incorrect signage are reported.
For Azione, this scenario does not represent the calling card of a province that, through the claim 'Land of Tourism', aims to attract visitors and enhance the territory. Participation in 'Lombardia si muove' thus becomes a denunciation of the critical state of the connection between the north of the Varese province, Milan, and Switzerland. The comparison between two trains per hour and four daily trips makes the difficulty for those commuting for work concrete. For a cross-border worker departing from Pino, Maccagno, Colmegna, or Luino, the S30 is described as suitable for short distances and strategic for reaching the Gotthard passenger services. However, the reduction indicated by Azione restricts travel possibilities and pushes users toward alternative means to find reliable connections with Milan or Switzerland.
### A problem that starts at the station
Taken together, the data outline three areas: availability of trips, speed of the Italian section, and station conditions. For the commuter, the hardship arises from the sum of these factors, not from a single element.
| Item | Reported Data | |---|---| | S30 Frequency | from two per hour to 4 daily trips | | Speed | 30 km/h on the Italian section | | Sought Connections | Milan or Switzerland | | Stations | Luino and Maccagno | | Line Use | freight and passenger traffic |
The first practical effect is reduced flexibility. Four daily trips, compared to two every hour, leave fewer opportunities to organize work-related travel; the press release links this exact situation to the need to resort to alternative means to find reliability. The line is not presented as marginal: it is included in the Alptransit and Rhine-Alpine corridors and is defined as strategic. The contrast between function and service is therefore the center of the criticism.
The second effect concerns the travel time. The figure of 30 km/h, defined as 'snail's pace', adds to the reduced frequency. For the worker, the result described by Azione is a connection that does not provide the efficiency expected by commuters.
The station also enters the daily evaluation: out-of-order elevators, broken displays, missing shelters, broken glass, and insufficient, obsolete, damaged, or incorrect signage are all critical issues reported for Luino and Maccagno. For those crossing the border for work, the journey also includes access and information. To navigate mobility alternatives, the [Ticino public transport](nav:transport) service is available.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). To transform the reported hardship into a public request, the path indicated by the press release can be followed in four steps. Stay within the perimeter of the mobilization: join the picket, pay attention to the Luino-Switzerland line, and support the signature collection.
### Four steps to participate
1. Mark the date: Saturday, September 26. This is the day when Azione will join the itinerant initiative of 'Lombardia si muove'.
2. Locate the mobilization in Lombardy stations, following the itinerant nature of the initiative. The picket brings together commuter committees and political representatives.
3. Join the signature collection promoted during the initiative. The goal is to demand an account of the progress of the works directly from the Minister of Transport.
4. Bring focus to the Luino-Switzerland route and the indicated conditions: S30 service, speed of the Italian section, connections for those departing from Pino, Maccagno, Colmegna, and Luino, and the state of the Luino and Maccagno stations.
These steps allow the cross-border worker to distinguish railway data from political evaluation. The mobilization does not generically ask for more attention: according to the press release, it aims to clarify why multi-million investments announced every year and hundreds of new trains purchased with public money have not avoided the critical issues of the local and regional service.
For those departing from the north of the province of Varese for work, the question to support is concrete: how can the Swiss-funded redevelopment be reconciled with a connection described as slow, infrequent, and marked by problems in the stations? The signature collection is the indicated tool to request an answer on the state of the works, without adding requests different from those of the source.
The commuter's contribution can remain linked to their own travel experience: the place of departure, the need to reach Milan or Switzerland, and the use of alternative means are the elements already mentioned in the press release. Before organizing the trip to the initiative, the worker can consult [Ticino public transport](nav:transport) to compare mobility options.
Participation remains anchored to Saturday, September 26, the signature collection, and the request regarding the state of the works. To continue navigating commuter travel options, consult [Ticino public transport](nav:transport).
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/09/azione-si-mobilita-per-un-sistema-ferroviario-efficiente-e-partecipa-al-presidio-di-lombardia-si-muove/2687080/)*
